generic.title: Review the finding and fix it
generic.explanation: Review the finding's evidence and apply the fix on the pages it affects.
generic.why: Any issue the audit finds can affect how search engines and AI tools read the site.
steps: Open the example page in the evidence and see the issue
Apply the fix on the affected pages
generic.verify: The next Maya audit no longer lists the finding.

blocked.title: The team report was not produced
blocked.RG-1: A card rests on a finding that is not in the report.
blocked.RG-2: A high-severity finding has no evidence.
blocked.RG-3: A card shows an address its findings do not list.
blocked.RG-4: A card shows something as confirmed that was not re-tested.
blocked.RG-5: A high-severity finding has no re-test state.
blocked.RG-6: A card refers to another card with no shared evidence.
blocked.RG-7: Content advice is given for a page of the wrong type.
blocked.RG-11: A card's title or step rests on a topic the report does not have.
blocked.RG-12: A validation count includes items that were not re-tested.
blocked.RG-14: No page of the site could be read; a new audit is needed, not a report.
blocked.RG-15: The report may have at most ten pages; this one is longer.
blocked.RG-16: The report may hold at most fifteen cards; this one has more.
blocked.RG-17: The appendix file does not hold every finding of the report.
blocked.gate: The release gate found a problem.
blocked.gate_missing: The release gate could not run, or the report changed after it was built; build the report again.
blocked.locked: A severity, a count or the card order was changed apart from the text.
blocked.unfilled: A text field was left empty.
blocked.empty: A text field was left empty.
blocked.length: A text does not fit its box.
blocked.steps: A card does not have two to four steps.
blocked.number: A text holds a number the report does not have.
blocked.address: A text names an address the report does not have.
blocked.language: A text is in the wrong language.
blocked.banned: A text holds a placeholder word.
blocked.table: One of the summary tables is over its limit.
blocked.overflow: A text does not fit its printed box.
blocked.pdf: The PDF check did not pass.
blocked.browser: The PDF could not be printed: the local browser (Chromium) was not found on this computer.
blocked.build: The report could not be built from this audit.

acc1.html.title: Serve robots.txt as plain text
acc1.html.finding: robots.txt answers with an HTML page
acc1.html.explanation: You should make the robots.txt address return a plain-text file with your crawler rules, not a web page.
acc1.html.why: A robots.txt address that answers with a web page gives crawlers no rules to read. Most then treat the site as having none.
steps: Open the robots.txt address in a browser and check what loads
Make the server return a plain-text robots.txt file
If you have no rules, return a not-found response instead
acc1.html.verify: Open the robots.txt address and check that plain-text rules load, not a web page.

acc1.large.title: Shrink robots.txt
acc1.large.explanation: You should cut robots.txt down by merging repeated rules and removing the ones that no longer apply.
acc1.large.why: Crawlers stop reading robots.txt past a size limit, so rules beyond that point can be ignored.
steps: Remove rules for paths that no longer exist
Merge repeated rules into shorter wildcard patterns
Keep the most important rules near the top
acc1.large.verify: Check the size of robots.txt in the browser's network panel; it should be well under Google's documented limit.

acc1.server_error.title: Make robots.txt load reliably
acc1.server_error.finding: robots.txt sometimes returns a server error
acc1.server_error.explanation: You should make the robots.txt address always return the file, or a not-found response if you have no rules.
acc1.server_error.why: Crawlers read robots.txt before anything else. When it fails to load, some stop and read nothing, and others treat the whole site as off-limits until it loads again.
steps: Check the server and CDN logs for errors on robots.txt
Serve robots.txt as a static file or from the CDN cache
If you have no rules, return a not-found response
acc1.server_error.verify: Check the robots.txt report in Search Console; the file should show as fetched, with no errors.

acc1.ungrouped.title: Move the stray robots.txt rule under a User-agent line
acc1.ungrouped.finding: robots.txt rules sit above any User-agent line
acc1.ungrouped.explanation: You should move each rule above the first User-agent line under the group it was meant for.
acc1.ungrouped.why: Rules written above the first User-agent line in robots.txt belong to no crawler, so a block the site meant to set is not set.
steps: Find the rule above the first User-agent line
Move it under the User-agent line it belongs to
acc1.ungrouped.verify: Open robots.txt and check that every rule sits under a User-agent line.

acc2.blocks.sample.title: Review the robots.txt rule that blocks crawlers
acc2.blocks.sample.finding: A robots.txt rule blocks some crawlers on some pages
acc2.blocks.sample.explanation: You should confirm whether the block is intended and, if not, narrow or remove the Disallow rule for these crawlers.
acc2.blocks.sample.why: Crawlers that robots.txt blocks cannot read those pages, so the search and AI answer engines they serve cannot show or quote them.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
If not, narrow the Disallow rule so it no longer matches these pages
Or add an Allow rule in these crawlers' own group
acc2.blocks.sample.verify: Check the affected addresses with Search Console's URL Inspection; crawling should show as allowed.

acc2.blocks.sitewide.title: Review the robots.txt rule that blocks crawlers sitewide
acc2.blocks.sitewide.finding: A robots.txt rule blocks some crawlers on the whole site
acc2.blocks.sitewide.explanation: You should confirm whether the sitewide block is intended and, if not, remove or narrow the Disallow rule for these crawlers.
acc2.blocks.sitewide.why: A sitewide block keeps these crawlers off every page, so the engines they serve cannot read, show or quote the site.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
If not, remove the whole-site Disallow rule from these crawlers' group
Keep blocks only on paths that must stay private
acc2.blocks.sitewide.verify: Open robots.txt and check these crawlers' group; the whole-site Disallow rule should be gone.

acc2.mismatch.title: Align robots.txt with your AI crawler policy
acc2.mismatch.finding: robots.txt allows crawlers the stated policy blocks
acc2.mismatch.explanation: You should add Disallow rules for these crawlers, or update the stated policy if allowing them is now intended.
acc2.mismatch.why: What the site says it wants for AI crawlers and what its robots.txt tells them are different. Crawlers follow the file.
steps: Confirm which policy is intended for these crawlers
To block them, add Disallow rules in their robots.txt groups
To allow them, update the stated policy instead
acc2.mismatch.verify: Open robots.txt and check that each named crawler's group matches the stated policy.

acc2.precedence.title: Repeat general robots.txt rules in crawler-specific groups
acc2.precedence.finding: A general robots.txt rule skips crawlers with their own group
acc2.precedence.explanation: If the general rule should also apply to these crawlers, you should repeat it inside each of their own groups.
acc2.precedence.why: A crawler with its own section in robots.txt ignores the general (*) rules. A rule you thought applied to everyone may not apply to it.
steps: Confirm whether the general rule should apply to these crawlers
If so, copy the rule into each crawler's own group
Recheck the file after each change
acc2.precedence.verify: Open robots.txt and check that each crawler-specific group holds the rules meant for all crawlers.

acc2.retired.title: Write robots.txt rules for the crawler names in use now
acc2.retired.finding: robots.txt has rules for crawler names no longer used
acc2.retired.explanation: You should repeat these rules for the crawler names the same companies use today; the old lines can stay but do nothing.
acc2.retired.why: Rules for a crawler name that is no longer used do nothing. A block the site meant to keep may not be in place for the crawler that replaced it.
steps: Find the rules written for retired crawler names
Look up the names that replaced them in each company's documentation
Write the same rules for the current names
acc2.retired.verify: Open robots.txt and check that each rule for a retired name also exists for its current name.

acc3.data_nosnippet.title: Take the main content out of data-nosnippet
acc3.data_nosnippet.explanation: You should remove the data-nosnippet attribute from the main content and keep it only on parts that must not be quoted.
acc3.data_nosnippet.why: Google does not quote text marked data-nosnippet in results or AI answers, so a page whose main text is marked has little to show.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Find the template element that carries data-nosnippet
Remove it from the main content and keep it only where needed
acc3.data_nosnippet.verify: View the page source and check that the main text is not inside an element with data-nosnippet.

acc3.max_snippet_low.title: Raise or remove the low max-snippet limit
acc3.max_snippet_low.finding: A max-snippet limit keeps snippets very short
acc3.max_snippet_low.explanation: You should raise the max-snippet value or remove it, unless very short snippets are intended.
acc3.max_snippet_low.why: A low max-snippet value caps how much text Google may quote, which leaves little for results and AI answers to show.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Find where it is set: the robots meta tag or the X-Robots-Tag header
Remove the value, or set it to no limit
acc3.max_snippet_low.verify: Check the robots meta tag and X-Robots-Tag header; no low max-snippet value should remain.

acc3.max_snippet_zero.title: Remove the max-snippet setting that blocks all snippets
acc3.max_snippet_zero.finding: max-snippet is set to allow no snippet at all
acc3.max_snippet_zero.explanation: You should remove the zero max-snippet value, unless you intend these pages never to be quoted.
acc3.max_snippet_zero.why: With max-snippet at zero, Google shows no text snippet for the page and does not use its text in AI answers.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Find where it is set: the robots meta tag or the X-Robots-Tag header
Remove the value, or set it to no limit
acc3.max_snippet_zero.verify: Check the robots meta tag and X-Robots-Tag header; max-snippet should no longer be set to zero.

acc3.noarchive.title: Review the noarchive setting
acc3.noarchive.explanation: You should remove noarchive unless you intend to keep Bing from using these pages in its AI answers.
acc3.noarchive.why: Bing reads noarchive as a request to keep the content out of its AI answers, so these pages may not be quoted in Copilot.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Find where it is set: the robots meta tag or the X-Robots-Tag header
Remove noarchive if the pages should be quoted
acc3.noarchive.verify: Check the page source and response headers; noarchive should no longer appear.

acc3.nocache.title: Review the nocache setting
acc3.nocache.explanation: You should remove nocache unless you intend Bing's AI answers to use only the title, address and snippet.
acc3.nocache.why: Bing reads nocache as a limit: its AI answers may use only the page's title, address and snippet, not the full text.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Find where it is set: the robots meta tag or the X-Robots-Tag header
Remove nocache if the full text should be usable
acc3.nocache.verify: Check the page source and response headers; nocache should no longer appear.

acc3.noindex.title: Confirm the noindex on these pages is intended
acc3.noindex.explanation: You should confirm each page should stay out of search, and remove the noindex from any page meant to be found.
acc3.noindex.why: A noindex keeps the page out of search results and AI answers, so engines will not show or quote it.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Remove the noindex from pages that should be found
Check theme, plugin or app settings that may add it
acc3.noindex.verify: Check the pages with Search Console's URL Inspection; pages meant to be found should show indexing allowed.

acc3.noindex_listed.title: Resolve noindex pages listed in the sitemap
acc3.noindex_listed.finding: Pages in the sitemap carry noindex
acc3.noindex_listed.explanation: You should either remove the noindex from these pages or take them out of the sitemap, whichever is intended.
acc3.noindex_listed.why: The sitemap asks engines to index these pages and the noindex tells them not to. The mixed signal can keep wanted pages out of search.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
If the pages should be found, remove the noindex
If not, take them out of the sitemap
acc3.noindex_listed.verify: Check Search Console's Pages report; no sitemap page should show as excluded by noindex.

acc3.noindex_utility.title: Confirm the noindex on utility pages is intended
acc3.noindex_utility.explanation: You should confirm these utility pages, such as print or QR menu pages, are meant to stay out of search.
acc3.noindex_utility.why: A noindex keeps a utility page out of search results. That is often intended, but a page people search for will not be found.
steps: Confirm whether the page should appear in search
If it should, remove the noindex
acc3.noindex_utility.verify: Check the pages with Search Console's URL Inspection; the indexing status should match your decision.

acc3.nosnippet.title: Remove nosnippet from pages that should be quoted
acc3.nosnippet.explanation: You should remove nosnippet unless you intend Google never to show or quote text from these pages.
acc3.nosnippet.why: With nosnippet, Google shows no text snippet for the page and does not use its text in AI answers.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Find where it is set: the robots meta tag or the X-Robots-Tag header
Remove nosnippet if the pages should be quoted
acc3.nosnippet.verify: Check the robots meta tag and X-Robots-Tag header; nosnippet should no longer appear.

acc3.robots_noindex.title: Let crawlers see the noindex, or drop it
acc3.robots_noindex.finding: Noindex pages are blocked in robots.txt
acc3.robots_noindex.explanation: You should choose per page: allow crawling so engines can see the noindex, or drop the noindex and keep the block.
acc3.robots_noindex.why: A crawler that robots.txt keeps out never reads the page, so it never sees the noindex either, and the address can stay in the index from links to it.
steps: Decide per page: leave the index, or stay uncrawled
To leave the index: allow it in robots.txt for now
To stay uncrawled: remove the noindex
acc3.robots_noindex.verify: Check the pages with Search Console's URL Inspection; crawling and indexing should match your choice.

acc3.robots_outside_head.title: Move the robots tag into the head
acc3.robots_outside_head.finding: A robots meta tag sits outside the head
acc3.robots_outside_head.explanation: You should move the robots meta tag into the <head> if it is meant, or remove it from the body if it is not.
acc3.robots_outside_head.why: Engines read robots instructions from the head. A tag in the body may be ignored by some and obeyed by others, so the result is hard to predict.
steps: Confirm whether the tag is intended
Find what adds it to the body, often a widget or embedded snippet
Move it into the <head>, or remove it if it is not meant
acc3.robots_outside_head.verify: View the page source and check that no robots meta tag appears after the <head> section closes.

acc3.sitemap_noindex.title: Take noindex pages out of the sitemap
acc3.sitemap_noindex.explanation: You should take these pages out of the sitemap if they are meant to stay out of search, or remove the noindex if not.
acc3.sitemap_noindex.why: A sitemap should list only pages you want indexed. Listing noindex pages sends engines a mixed signal and wastes their visits.
steps: Confirm whether the noindex is intended
If so, remove these pages from the sitemap
If not, remove the noindex from the pages
acc3.sitemap_noindex.verify: Check Search Console's Sitemaps and Pages reports; no submitted page should show as excluded by noindex.

acc3.unavailable_future.title: Confirm the unavailable_after date is intended
acc3.unavailable_future.explanation: You should confirm these pages should leave Google on that date, and remove the setting from any page meant to stay.
acc3.unavailable_future.why: After the unavailable_after date, Google drops the page from its results as if it carried noindex.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Remove the setting from pages that should stay in search
Update the date where the content is still current
acc3.unavailable_future.verify: Check the robots meta tag and X-Robots-Tag header; only pages meant to expire should carry the date.

acc3.unavailable_listed.title: Resolve expired pages listed in the sitemap
acc3.unavailable_listed.finding: Sitemap pages have a past unavailable_after date
acc3.unavailable_listed.explanation: You should remove the expired setting from pages meant to be found, or take those pages out of the sitemap.
acc3.unavailable_listed.why: A past unavailable_after date works like noindex, while the sitemap asks for indexing. The mixed signal can keep wanted pages out of search.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
If the pages should be found, remove the unavailable_after setting
If not, take them out of the sitemap
acc3.unavailable_listed.verify: Check Search Console's Pages report; sitemap pages meant to be found should show as indexed.

acc3.unavailable_passed.title: Remove the expired unavailable_after setting
acc3.unavailable_passed.finding: Pages have a past unavailable_after date
acc3.unavailable_passed.explanation: You should remove the unavailable_after setting from pages that should still appear in search.
acc3.unavailable_passed.why: Once the unavailable_after date has passed, Google treats the page like a noindex page and drops it from results.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Remove the setting from pages that should still be found
Check the template or app that adds the date
acc3.unavailable_passed.verify: Check the pages with Search Console's URL Inspection; pages meant to be found should show indexing allowed.

acc3.utility_indexable.title: Keep internal search and cart pages out of the index
acc3.utility_indexable.finding: Internal search and cart pages can be indexed
acc3.utility_indexable.explanation: You should add a noindex robots tag to internal search and cart pages, and keep them out of the sitemap.
acc3.utility_indexable.why: Search result and cart pages are endless, near-empty variations. Indexing them wastes crawler visits and can crowd out real pages.
steps: Add a noindex robots tag to the search and cart pages
Keep these pages out of the sitemap
acc3.utility_indexable.verify: Open the source of the internal search and cart pages; a noindex robots tag should appear there.

Shopify: Add a noindex robots tag to the search and cart pages
On Shopify: in the theme's <head>, for the search and cart templates
Keep these pages out of the sitemap

acc4.different.title: Serve crawlers the same content as browsers
acc4.different.finding: Crawlers get different content than browsers
acc4.different.explanation: You should compare what the bot and the browser receive and, unless the difference is intended, serve both the same page.
acc4.different.why: When crawlers get different content than visitors, engines read and quote something visitors never see, or miss the real page.
steps: Confirm whether the difference is intended
Compare the bot and browser responses for the same address
Fix the firewall, CDN or cache rule that serves the bot another page
acc4.different.verify: Fetch one affected address with a crawler user agent and with a browser; both should get the same content.

acc4.outcome.title: Let AI and search crawlers through bot protection
acc4.outcome.finding: Bot protection turns away crawler requests
acc4.outcome.explanation: You should allow these crawlers in the firewall, bot-protection and rate-limit rules, checking real bots by their published IP ranges.
acc4.outcome.why: A firewall can turn AI and search crawlers away even when robots.txt allows them, so the engines they serve cannot read the site.
steps: Confirm whether the block is intended
Allow these crawlers in the firewall, bot-protection and rate-limit rules
Check real bots by their published IP ranges, not the user agent alone
acc4.outcome.verify: Check the firewall or CDN logs for these crawlers; their requests should get the page, not a block or challenge.

acc4.redirected.title: Stop redirecting crawlers elsewhere
acc4.redirected.finding: Crawlers are redirected where browsers are not
acc4.redirected.explanation: You should find the rule that redirects crawler user agents and let them reach the same address a browser does.
acc4.redirected.why: A crawler sent somewhere other than the page reads the wrong content, so engines may index or quote the wrong address.
steps: Confirm whether the redirect is intended
Find the firewall, CDN or app rule that redirects these user agents
Let them reach the same address a browser does
acc4.redirected.verify: Fetch one affected address with a crawler user agent; it should land on the same address as a browser.

acc4.ua_check.challenged.title: Check that the real Googlebot is not challenged
acc4.ua_check.challenged.finding: Requests posing as Googlebot were challenged
acc4.ua_check.challenged.explanation: You should check Search Console crawl stats for refused answers to the real Googlebot, and change nothing if there are none.
acc4.ua_check.challenged.why: Firewalls often challenge fake Googlebots on purpose. That is fine, as long as the real Googlebot from its verified addresses gets through.
steps: Open Search Console crawl stats and group them by response
Look for refused or rate-limited answers to the real Googlebot
If there are any, allow Googlebot's verified IPs in the firewall
acc4.ua_check.challenged.verify: Check Search Console crawl stats by response; the real Googlebot should get no refused or challenged answers.

acc4.ua_check.empty.title: Serve Googlebot the full page
acc4.ua_check.empty.finding: Googlebot's user agent gets an empty page
acc4.ua_check.empty.explanation: You should find what sends Googlebot's user agent an empty page and make it receive the same page a browser gets.
acc4.ua_check.empty.why: If the real Googlebot gets an empty page, Google has nothing to index or show for that address.
steps: Check one affected address with Search Console's URL Inspection
Find the bot filter, firewall or cache rule that serves the empty page
Make Googlebot receive the same page a browser gets
acc4.ua_check.empty.verify: Run a live test in Search Console's URL Inspection; the fetched page should show the full content.

acc4.ua_check.size.title: Check why Googlebot gets a different page size
acc4.ua_check.size.finding: Googlebot's user agent gets a page of very different size
acc4.ua_check.size.explanation: You should compare what Googlebot's user agent and a browser receive, and confirm the difference is harmless.
acc4.ua_check.size.why: A large size gap can mean Googlebot gets a cut-down or different page, so Google may index less than visitors see.
steps: Confirm whether the difference is intended
Compare the two responses for one affected address
If content is missing for Googlebot, fix the rule that removes it
acc4.ua_check.size.verify: Run a live test in Search Console's URL Inspection; the fetched HTML should hold the content a browser sees.

acc4.ua_check.status.title: Let Googlebot's requests through the firewall
acc4.ua_check.status.finding: Googlebot's user agent gets a different response code
acc4.ua_check.status.explanation: You should let Googlebot's verified requests through the firewall so they get the same answer a browser does.
acc4.ua_check.status.why: If the real Googlebot is refused, Google cannot crawl these pages and may drop them from its results.
steps: Allow Googlebot's verified IPs in the firewall
Test it with Search Console's URL Inspection
acc4.ua_check.status.verify: Check Search Console's URL Inspection and crawl stats; the real Googlebot should get the same answer as a browser.

acc5.never.title: Help search crawlers reach these pages
acc5.never.finding: No verified search crawler fetched these pages
acc5.never.explanation: You should check the internal links and sitemap entries for these pages, and look again with a longer log window.
acc5.never.why: Server logs show which pages search crawlers really visit. Pages they never fetch are not refreshed in the index.
steps: Check that the pages are linked from other pages on the site
Check that they are listed in the sitemap
Look again with a longer log window
acc5.never.verify: Check Search Console crawl stats or the server logs; verified search crawlers should fetch these pages.

acc6.scope.title: Review your choices for each AI crawler role
acc6.scope.finding: AI crawler access differs by role
acc6.scope.explanation: You should confirm that each AI company's training, search and live-fetch crawlers are allowed or blocked as you intend.
acc6.scope.why: Blocking a training crawler and a search crawler are different choices. Blocking a search crawler can keep the site out of that company's AI answers.
steps: Confirm whether each block is intended
Check each company's crawler names for training, search and live fetch
Give each crawler name its own robots.txt group
acc6.scope.verify: Open robots.txt and check each AI crawler's group against your intended choice for training, search and live fetch.

acc7.capped.title: Lower the crawl delay so the next audit can read more
acc7.capped.finding: The crawl delay limited how much the audit read
acc7.capped.explanation: If you want the next audit to read more pages, you should lower or remove the Crawl-delay that applies to all crawlers.
acc7.capped.why: The site asked this audit to slow down. The audit obeyed, which limited how many pages it could read in the time it had.
steps: Confirm whether the long delay is intended
Lower or remove the Crawl-delay in the group that applies to all crawlers
Run the audit again after the change
acc7.capped.verify: Open robots.txt and check the Crawl-delay value in the group that applies to all crawlers.

acc7.delay.title: Lower or remove the Crawl-delay
acc7.delay.finding: robots.txt sets a crawl delay for some crawlers
acc7.delay.explanation: You should lower or remove the Crawl-delay for these crawlers if you want new and changed pages picked up quickly.
acc7.delay.why: A long crawl delay means a crawler reads only a small part of the site in each visit, so new and changed pages are picked up late.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Lower or remove the Crawl-delay line in these crawlers' groups
Use server rate limits instead if server load is the concern
acc7.delay.verify: Open robots.txt and check that these crawlers' groups have no long Crawl-delay.

acc8.links.title: Fix the broken links in llms.txt
acc8.links.finding: llms.txt links lead to pages that do not work
acc8.links.explanation: You should replace each broken link in llms.txt with the working address, or remove it.
acc8.links.why: An AI tool that follows llms.txt is sent to pages that are gone, empty or moved, so the file points it away from the site's real content.
steps: Open each link listed in llms.txt
Replace moved addresses with their final address
Remove links to pages that are gone or empty
acc8.links.verify: Open every link in llms.txt; each should load a working page with content.

acc8.links.idx1.title: Fix llms.txt links to broken and empty pages
acc8.links.idx1.finding: llms.txt links lead to broken or empty pages
acc8.links.idx1.explanation: You should fix the empty pages these links lead to, and replace or remove the other broken links in llms.txt.
acc8.links.idx1.why: An AI tool that follows llms.txt is sent to pages that are gone, empty or moved, so the file points it away from the site's real content.
steps: Fix the empty pages first, as search crawlers get nothing from them either
Replace moved addresses with their final address
Remove links to pages that are gone
acc8.links.idx1.verify: Open every link in llms.txt; each should load a working page with content.

acc8.no_title.title: Start llms.txt with a title line
acc8.no_title.explanation: You should start llms.txt with one title line holding the site's name, as the llms.txt proposal describes.
acc8.no_title.why: The llms.txt proposal opens the file with the site's name as a title line. A tool that reads it that way may not find the name.
steps: Open llms.txt in an editor
Add a first line made of a hash sign, a space and the site's name
Keep the rest of the file below it
acc8.no_title.verify: Open the llms.txt address; the first line should be a hash sign followed by the site's name.

acc8.present.title: Keep llms.txt current
acc8.present.finding: The site publishes an llms.txt file
acc8.present.explanation: You should keep llms.txt in step with the site; it is optional and no major answer engine documents using it.
acc8.present.why: llms.txt is an optional file some sites publish for AI tools. No major answer engine documents using it, so it is recorded, not scored.
steps: Check that its links point to current pages
Update it when key pages change
Keep the sitemap as the main list of pages for crawlers
acc8.present.verify: Open the llms.txt address; it should load and list current, working pages.

acc8.redirecting.title: Point llms.txt links at their final addresses
acc8.redirecting.finding: llms.txt links point to addresses that redirect
acc8.redirecting.explanation: You should replace each listed address in llms.txt with the address it redirects to.
acc8.redirecting.why: Each redirect is an extra step for a tool reading llms.txt, and some tools may not follow it to the real page.
steps: Open each llms.txt link and note where it lands
Replace the link with that final address
Recheck the file after the change
acc8.redirecting.verify: Open each link in llms.txt; it should load directly, with no redirect.

acc9.blocked.title: Let honest crawlers through bot protection
acc9.blocked.finding: Bot protection blocks or challenges automated visitors
acc9.blocked.explanation: You should decide whether this protection is meant for crawlers, and allow the AI and search crawlers you want to reach you.
acc9.blocked.why: When protection turns away a crawler that says who it is, AI search and assistant crawlers may be turned away too and cannot read or quote the site.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Check the firewall or bot-protection rules that answered these requests
Allow the AI and search crawlers you want, checked by their published IP ranges
acc9.blocked.verify: Check the firewall or CDN logs; named AI and search crawlers should receive pages, not blocks or challenges.

acc9.blocked_429.title: Stop refusing page requests from honest crawlers
acc9.blocked_429.finding: Page requests get a too-many-requests answer
acc9.blocked_429.explanation: You should check the bot and rate-limit rules that refuse page requests while robots.txt and the sitemap load, and allow honest crawlers.
acc9.blocked_429.why: When protection turns away a crawler that says who it is, AI search and assistant crawlers may be turned away too and cannot read or quote the site.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Find the bot or rate-limit rule that refuses page requests
Allow the audit's crawler and the AI crawlers you want, then run the audit again
acc9.blocked_429.verify: Check the firewall or CDN logs; page requests from named crawlers should get pages, not too-many-requests answers.

acc9.rate_limited_429.title: Relax the rate limit for honest crawlers
acc9.rate_limited_429.finding: Page requests hit the site's rate limit
acc9.rate_limited_429.explanation: You should check the rate-limit rules that refuse page requests and give known crawlers a higher limit.
acc9.rate_limited_429.why: When protection turns away a crawler that says who it is, AI search and assistant crawlers may be turned away too and cannot read or quote the site.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Find the rate-limit rule that refuses these page requests
Give the audit's crawler and the AI crawlers you want a higher limit
acc9.rate_limited_429.verify: Check the firewall or CDN logs; page requests from named crawlers should get pages, not too-many-requests answers.

acc9.reader.title: Allow the audit's crawler so the next audit can read the site directly
acc9.reader.finding: The audit's direct crawler was turned away
acc9.reader.explanation: So the next audit can read more and measure crawler access, you should allow Maya's user agent in the bot-protection rules.
acc9.reader.why: Bot protection turned away the audit's own crawler, so pages were read another way and real AI crawler access could not be measured.
steps: Decide with the site owner whether the protection is meant for crawlers
Allow Maya's user agent in the firewall or bot-protection rules
Run the audit again
acc9.reader.verify: Check the firewall or bot-protection logs; requests with Maya's user agent should get pages, not blocks.

acc9.reader.counted.title: Allow the audit's crawler so the next audit can read the site directly
acc9.reader.counted.finding: The audit's direct crawler was turned away on some requests
acc9.reader.counted.explanation: So the next audit can read more and measure crawler access, you should allow Maya's user agent in the bot-protection rules.
acc9.reader.counted.why: Bot protection turned away the audit's own crawler, so pages were read another way and real AI crawler access could not be measured.
steps: Decide with the site owner whether the protection is meant for crawlers
Allow Maya's user agent in the firewall or bot-protection rules
Run the audit again
acc9.reader.counted.verify: Check the firewall or bot-protection logs; requests with Maya's user agent should get pages, not blocks.

acc9.reader.site.title: Allow the audit's crawler so the next audit can read the site directly
acc9.reader.site.finding: The site's bot protection turned the audit's crawler away
acc9.reader.site.explanation: So the next audit can read more and measure crawler access, you should allow Maya's user agent in the bot-protection rules.
acc9.reader.site.why: Bot protection turned away the audit's own crawler, so pages were read another way and real AI crawler access could not be measured.
steps: Decide with the site owner whether the protection is meant for crawlers
Allow Maya's user agent in the firewall or bot-protection rules
Run the audit again
acc9.reader.site.verify: Check the firewall or bot-protection logs; requests with Maya's user agent should get pages, not blocks.

acc9.reader.site.counted.title: Allow the audit's crawler so the next audit can read the site directly
acc9.reader.site.counted.finding: Bot protection turned the audit's crawler away at times
acc9.reader.site.counted.explanation: So the next audit can read more and measure crawler access, you should allow Maya's user agent in the bot-protection rules.
acc9.reader.site.counted.why: Bot protection turned away the audit's own crawler, so pages were read another way and real AI crawler access could not be measured.
steps: Decide with the site owner whether the protection is meant for crawlers
Allow Maya's user agent in the firewall or bot-protection rules
Run the audit again
acc9.reader.site.counted.verify: Check the firewall or bot-protection logs; requests with Maya's user agent should get pages, not blocks.

ans1.fails.title: Fix the site issues on cited pages
ans1.fails.finding: A page AI answers cite fails a site check
ans1.fails.explanation: You should fix the site check failures on this cited page first, since answer engines already use it.
ans1.fails.why: Answer engines already cite this page. If it cannot be read or indexed well, they may stop citing it or show outdated content.
steps: Open the site findings listed for this address
Fix those issues on the page first
Recheck the page after the change
ans1.fails.verify: Open the cited address in a browser and in Search Console's URL Inspection; it should load and be indexable.

ans2.contradicts.title: Update pages that AI answers contradict
ans2.contradicts.finding: AI answers state facts the cited page contradicts
ans2.contradicts.explanation: You should check each conflict and, if the page is out of date, update it along with its structured data and lastmod.
ans2.contradicts.why: When answers repeat facts that differ from the cited page, readers get wrong information credited to the site.
steps: Compare each answer with the cited page
If the page is out of date, update it, its structured data and lastmod
If the page is right, note the answer as stale or drawn from elsewhere
ans2.contradicts.verify: Open the cited page and check that the facts it states are current and match its structured data.

ans2.not_shown.title: Check answer claims the cited page does not show
ans2.not_shown.finding: AI answers make claims the cited page does not show
ans2.not_shown.explanation: You should read each claim against the cited page, and add the fact to the page if it should state it.
ans2.not_shown.why: The answer credits the site with a claim the page does not make. It may come from elsewhere, or the page may have dropped the fact.
steps: Read each claim against the cited page
If the page should state it, add it in plain words
If the answer is wrong, treat it as a content question for that page
ans2.not_shown.verify: Open the cited page and check that every fact you want cited is stated there in plain words.

ans4.none_from_site.title: Find out why this engine does not cite the site
ans4.none_from_site.finding: An answer engine cites others on this topic, not this site
ans4.none_from_site.explanation: You should first check that this engine's crawlers are allowed, then compare the pages it cites with the site's own page on the topic.
ans4.none_from_site.why: Engines cite sites they can read and that answer the question well. Missing citations point to an access or content gap.
steps: Check that robots.txt and the firewall allow this engine's crawlers
Compare the cited pages with the site's own page on the topic
Fill the content gaps you find on the site's page
ans4.none_from_site.verify: Check robots.txt and the firewall logs; this engine's crawlers should be allowed and receive pages.

idx1.4xx.referenced.title: Fix or remove links to pages that return an error
idx1.4xx.referenced.finding: Linked or listed addresses return an error
idx1.4xx.referenced.explanation: You should restore each page that should exist, or point its links elsewhere and take it out of the sitemap.
idx1.4xx.referenced.why: A link or sitemap entry that leads to a missing page wastes a crawler's visit and sends visitors to an error.
steps: Find the links to the failing addresses
Point them at the right address or remove them
Take the addresses out of the sitemap
idx1.4xx.referenced.verify: Recrawl the site or run a link checker; no internal link or sitemap entry should lead to an error.

idx1.4xx.referenced.linked.title: Fix or remove links to pages that return an error
idx1.4xx.referenced.linked.finding: Pages link to addresses that return an error
idx1.4xx.referenced.linked.explanation: You should restore each page that should exist, or point its links elsewhere and take it out of the sitemap.
idx1.4xx.referenced.linked.why: A link or sitemap entry that leads to a missing page wastes a crawler's visit and sends visitors to an error.
steps: Find the links to the failing addresses
Point them at the right address or remove them
Take the addresses out of the sitemap
idx1.4xx.referenced.linked.verify: Recrawl the site or run a link checker; no internal link or sitemap entry should lead to an error.

idx1.4xx.unreferenced.title: Check the error addresses no page links to
idx1.4xx.unreferenced.explanation: You should check where these addresses come from, and redirect any that once held content to the closest page.
idx1.4xx.unreferenced.why: Nothing on the site links to these addresses, so the harm is small. Old links from other sites may still lead visitors to them.
steps: Check Search Console for where these addresses are linked from
Redirect any that once held content to the closest page
Leave the rest as not-found responses
idx1.4xx.unreferenced.verify: Check Search Console's Pages report; these addresses should show as redirected or not found, as you chose.

idx1.5xx.title: Fix pages that return a server error
idx1.5xx.finding: Pages return a server error every time
idx1.5xx.explanation: You should check the server logs for these addresses and fix the error, or return a not-found response for pages that are gone.
idx1.5xx.why: A page that answers with a server error cannot be read, indexed or quoted, and repeated errors make crawlers visit less often.
steps: Check the server logs for these addresses
Fix the error behind them
If a page is gone, return a not-found response or redirect it
idx1.5xx.verify: Open each address in a browser and in Search Console's URL Inspection; each should load without a server error.

idx1.5xx.once.title: Recheck pages that returned a server error once
idx1.5xx.once.finding: Pages returned a server error on one request
idx1.5xx.once.explanation: You should request these addresses again and check the server logs at the recorded time to see if the error repeats.
idx1.5xx.once.why: A page that answers with a server error cannot be read, indexed or quoted, and repeated errors make crawlers visit less often.
steps: Request these addresses again
Check the server logs at the recorded time
If the error repeats, fix it; if a page is gone, return a not-found response
idx1.5xx.once.verify: Open each address a few times in a browser; each should load every time without a server error.

idx1.connection.title: Fix addresses that cannot be connected to
idx1.connection.explanation: You should check the server, DNS and firewall settings for these addresses so that connections succeed.
idx1.connection.why: A page that cannot be connected to does not exist as far as a crawler is concerned, so it cannot be indexed or quoted.
steps: Check that the host name resolves and the server is running
Check firewall rules that may drop connections
Check the server and network logs at the failed times
idx1.connection.verify: Open each address from another network; it should connect and load the page.

idx1.empty.title: Fix pages that answer with an empty page
idx1.empty.finding: Pages answer with an empty response
idx1.empty.explanation: You should request these addresses again with the same client and, if they stay empty, find what sends no content.
idx1.empty.why: An empty response gives crawlers nothing to read, index or quote for that address.
steps: Request these addresses again and confirm the response is still empty
Check the server error log and any security or cache plugin
If a page should not exist, return a not-found response
idx1.empty.verify: Open each address with a crawler user agent; the response should hold the page's content.

idx1.empty.bot.title: Stop sending empty pages to automated clients
idx1.empty.bot.finding: Pages are empty for automated clients only
idx1.empty.bot.explanation: You should find the bot filter, firewall, CDN or cache rule that sends automated clients an empty answer, and fix it.
idx1.empty.bot.why: Crawlers that get an empty page have nothing to index or quote, while visitors see the full page.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Find the bot filter, firewall, CDN or cache rule behind it
Let crawlers that should read the site get the page a browser gets
idx1.empty.bot.verify: Open each address with a crawler user agent; the response should match what a browser gets.

idx1.error_text.title: Hide server error messages and file paths
idx1.error_text.explanation: You should turn off error display on the live server, log errors instead, and fix the error itself.
idx1.error_text.why: An error message on a live page shows visitors how the server is built, and engines may read the error text as the page's content.
steps: Turn off error display to visitors
Fix the error itself from the server log
idx1.error_text.verify: Open the affected pages; no error message or server file path should appear.

WordPress: Set WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY to false in wp-config.php
Fix the error shown in the debug log

idx1.soft404.200.title: Return a real not-found answer for missing pages
idx1.soft404.200.finding: Missing pages answer as if they exist
idx1.soft404.200.explanation: You should make addresses that do not exist return a not-found response, with a helpful error page.
idx1.soft404.200.why: When a missing address answers as if it were a real page, engines cannot tell real pages from mistakes and may index empty ones.
steps: Open a made-up address on the site and check the response
Set the server or platform to return a not-found status for it
Keep a helpful not-found page with links to the main sections
idx1.soft404.200.verify: Open a made-up address with the browser's network panel open; the status should be not found.

idx1.soft404.redirect.title: Answer addresses that do not exist with a real not-found
idx1.soft404.redirect.finding: Missing pages redirect to the homepage
idx1.soft404.redirect.explanation: You should stop redirecting missing addresses to the homepage and answer them with a real not-found page.
idx1.soft404.redirect.why: When a missing address answers as if it were a real page, engines cannot tell real pages from mistakes and may index empty ones.
steps: Stop sending missing addresses to the homepage
Show them a real not-found page instead
idx1.soft404.redirect.verify: Open a made-up address with the browser's network panel open; it should not redirect and the status should be not found.

idx1.timeout.title: Fix pages that time out
idx1.timeout.finding: Pages time out on every attempt
idx1.timeout.explanation: You should find what makes these addresses hang, such as slow queries, locks or slow outside services, and fix it.
idx1.timeout.why: A page that never answers in time is given up on by crawlers, as it would be by a visitor.
steps: Open the addresses and time how long they take
Check the server and outside service logs at the failed times
Fix the slow query, lock or service that holds the answer
idx1.timeout.verify: Open each address with the browser's network panel open; it should answer quickly and load fully.

idx10.bing_error.title: Fix key pages Bing could not fetch
idx10.bing_error.finding: Bing's last crawl of key pages got an error
idx10.bing_error.explanation: You should check that these pages load now, and resubmit them in Bing Webmaster Tools.
idx10.bing_error.why: Bing's index also feeds several AI assistants. A page Bing could not fetch is missing from all of them.
steps: Open each page and check that it loads
Fix any error you still find
Resubmit the pages in Bing Webmaster Tools
idx10.bing_error.verify: Use URL Inspection in Bing Webmaster Tools; the last crawl should show the page fetched without an error.

idx10.indexnow.title: Publish the IndexNow key file
idx10.indexnow.finding: The IndexNow key file is missing or does not match
idx10.indexnow.explanation: You should publish the IndexNow key file at its key location, holding exactly the key your site sends.
idx10.indexnow.why: IndexNow tells Bing and others about changed pages at once. With a missing or wrong key file, those notices are ignored.
steps: Find the IndexNow key your site or app uses
Publish a text file holding that key at the key location
Check that the file loads and matches the key
idx10.indexnow.verify: Open the key file address in a browser; it should show exactly the key your site sends.

idx2.expires.title: Renew the TLS certificate
idx2.expires.explanation: You should renew the certificate now, and check that automatic renewal is working.
idx2.expires.why: When the certificate expires, browsers show a warning and crawlers stop reading the site until it is renewed.
steps: Renew the certificate with your host or certificate provider
Turn on or fix automatic renewal
Check every host name the certificate must cover
idx2.expires.verify: Open the site and view the certificate details in the browser; the expiry date should be well in the future.

idx2.invalid.title: Fix the invalid TLS certificate
idx2.invalid.finding: The TLS certificate is not valid
idx2.invalid.explanation: You should reissue the certificate so it covers each host name, including www, and install the full chain.
idx2.invalid.why: With an invalid certificate, browsers show a warning and most crawlers refuse to read the site at all.
steps: Read the error message to see what is wrong
Reissue the certificate to cover every host name, with and without www
Install the full certificate chain on the server
idx2.invalid.verify: Open each host name in a browser; no certificate warning should appear.

idx2.no_redirect.title: Redirect http to https
idx2.no_redirect.finding: The http address does not redirect to https
idx2.no_redirect.explanation: You should redirect every http address to its https version with a permanent redirect, on each host name.
idx2.no_redirect.why: Without a redirect, the http and https addresses are two copies of the site, and visitors who type the http one get an insecure page.
steps: Turn on the http to https redirect in the server, CDN or host settings
Use a permanent redirect on each host name
Update internal links to the https addresses
idx2.no_redirect.verify: Open the http address of each host name; it should land on the https address in one step.

idx2.no_redirect.hosts.title: Redirect http to https
idx2.no_redirect.hosts.finding: The http address does not redirect to https
idx2.no_redirect.hosts.explanation: You should redirect every http address to its https version with a permanent redirect, on each host name.
idx2.no_redirect.hosts.why: Without a redirect, the http and https addresses are two copies of the site, and visitors who type the http one get an insecure page.
steps: Turn on the http to https redirect in the server, CDN or host settings
Use a permanent redirect on each host name
Update internal links to the https addresses
idx2.no_redirect.hosts.verify: Open the http address of each host name; it should land on the https address in one step.

idx2.temporary.title: Make the http to https redirect permanent
idx2.temporary.finding: The http to https redirect is temporary
idx2.temporary.explanation: You should change the http to https redirect to a permanent one on each host name.
idx2.temporary.why: A temporary redirect says the move is not for good, so engines may keep the http address as the one they index.
steps: Make the http to https redirect permanent
Apply it on every host name, with and without www
idx2.temporary.verify: Open the http address with the browser's network panel open; the redirect should be marked permanent.

idx3.chain.title: Shorten the redirect chains
idx3.chain.explanation: You should redirect the first address straight to the final one, and point internal links at the final address.
idx3.chain.why: Each extra redirect is another request before the page appears. Crawlers follow only a few and may give up.
steps: Redirect the first address straight to the last
Update internal links to the final address
idx3.chain.verify: Open the first address with the browser's network panel open; it should reach the final page in one redirect.

idx3.cookie.title: Make pages load without a cookie
idx3.cookie.finding: Pages loop when no cookie is sent
idx3.cookie.explanation: You should compare the cookie-less and cookie requests, and make the page load for visitors that keep no cookie.
idx3.cookie.why: Crawlers usually keep no cookies. If a page only loads once a cookie is set, they may go round in a loop and never read it.
steps: Confirm whether the cookie wall is intended
Compare the cookie-less and cookie requests in the server logs
Serve the page to cookie-less visitors and show any wall over it
idx3.cookie.verify: Open the address in a private window with cookies blocked; the page should load without a loop.

idx3.intermittent.title: Stop pages redirecting to themselves
idx3.intermittent.explanation: You should compare the successful and looping requests, and remove the rule that sends the address back to itself.
idx3.intermittent.why: A request that is sent back to the same address is wasted. Crawlers that get it often enough may read the page less often.
steps: Compare successful and looping requests in the server logs
Find the cause before changing the setup
Fix the redirect rule, then test the address again
idx3.intermittent.verify: Request the address several times with the network panel open; it should load each time with no redirect to itself.

idx3.loop.title: Fix the redirect loops
idx3.loop.explanation: You should check the server logs for the looping requests, find the cause and fix the rules so each address ends at a real page.
idx3.loop.why: A redirect loop never reaches a page, so crawlers and visitors who hit it get nothing to read.
steps: Check the server request logs for the looping addresses
Find the rule that sends them round in a circle
Fix it so each address ends at a real page, then test with and without cookies
idx3.loop.verify: Open the address with the browser's network panel open; it should end at a page that loads, with no loop.

idx3.other_host.title: Review redirects that lead to another domain
idx3.other_host.finding: Some pages redirect to another domain
idx3.other_host.explanation: Confirm each redirect is intended, and have the target domain checked in an audit of its own.
idx3.other_host.why: The page a visitor finally lands on was not read in this audit. Problems there can still affect search and AI answer engines.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
If not, redirect the page to the right address on your own domain
Have the target domain checked in a separate audit
idx3.other_host.verify: Open the redirecting address in a browser; for an intended move, the target page should load cleanly.

idx3.self_once.title: Recheck the redirect cycles
idx3.self_once.finding: A redirect cycle was seen on some addresses
idx3.self_once.explanation: Open the addresses again to confirm whether the cycle persists, and fix the redirect rule if it does.
idx3.self_once.why: A redirect that returns to itself leads crawlers to no page. If the cycle persists, the page cannot be indexed.
steps: Open the addresses again in a browser and with curl, without cookies
Find the source of the redirects in the server or CDN log
If the cycle persists, make the rule end at one final address
idx3.self_once.verify: Open the address with curl; the redirects should end at a page, not return to the same address.

idx3.to_http.title: Redirect to the https address
idx3.to_http.finding: Some pages redirect from https to an http address
idx3.to_http.explanation: Make each redirect point straight at the https address and remove the detour through http.
idx3.to_http.why: A redirect to an insecure http address weakens the secure version engines prefer and adds an extra step.
steps: Write the https address as the redirect target
If the http address redirects back to https, remove that detour
idx3.to_http.verify: Open the old address with curl; the redirect should end directly at an https page.

idx4.broken.title: Fix canonicals that point at broken pages
idx4.broken.finding: Canonical points at a broken or noindexed page
idx4.broken.explanation: Point the canonical at a working, indexable address, which is usually the page's own address.
idx4.broken.why: The canonical names the version that should be indexed. When it points at a page that cannot be indexed, neither may be.
steps: Open the canonical target and check it for an error or noindex
Write the page's own address, or a working correct one, as canonical
Fix the template that writes the wrong address
idx4.broken.verify: The address named by the canonical tag in the page source should load without error and carry no noindex.

idx4.conflict.title: Keep a single canonical declaration
idx4.conflict.explanation: Declare the canonical in one place, in the HTML or an HTTP header, and remove or align the others.
idx4.conflict.why: Two different canonical signals leave the engine to choose, and it may choose neither.
steps: List the canonical tags in the HTML and in the HTTP headers
Keep one declaration
Remove the others or make them name the same address
idx4.conflict.verify: The page source and the response headers should show a single canonical declaration.

idx4.different.title: Point canonicals at pages with the same content
idx4.different.finding: Canonical points at a page with different content
idx4.different.explanation: If the page's own content should be cited, make it its own canonical; otherwise confirm the canonical is intended.
idx4.different.why: Engines that honor the canonical index the target instead of this page, so its own text does not appear in search or AI answers.
steps: Open the canonical target and compare the content
If it differs, make the page its own canonical
idx4.different.verify: Open the canonical address from the page source; it should show the same content or be the page itself.

idx4.mixed.title: Choose between noindex and the canonical
idx4.mixed.finding: Pages carry noindex and a canonical to another address
idx4.mixed.explanation: Remove noindex to fold the page into its target, or keep noindex and make the page its own canonical.
idx4.mixed.why: noindex beside a canonical to another address sends engines mixed signals, and the engine picks which one to follow.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
To fold the page into its target, remove noindex and keep the canonical
To keep it out of the index, make the page its own canonical
idx4.mixed.verify: The page source should show either noindex or a canonical to another address, never both.

idx4.other_site.title: Review canonicals that point at another site
idx4.other_site.explanation: Unless the content is knowingly shared from that site, write the page's own address as the canonical.
idx4.other_site.why: A canonical pointing at another site tells engines to credit that site for this page's content.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
If not, write the page's own address as canonical
Fix the template or plugin that writes the other domain
idx4.other_site.verify: Outside intended sharing, the canonical tag in the page source should name the page's own domain.

idx4.redirect_loop.title: Make the canonical the page's own address
idx4.redirect_loop.finding: Canonical redirects back to the page itself
idx4.redirect_loop.explanation: Write the page's own final address, one that opens without a redirect, as the canonical.
idx4.redirect_loop.why: The canonical sends engines to another address and the redirect sends them back, so the page never states which address it prefers.
steps: Write the page's own final address as canonical
Fix the template that writes the other address
idx4.redirect_loop.verify: Open the canonical address from the page source with curl; it should answer with the page, without a redirect.

idx4.redirecting.title: Point the canonical at the final address
idx4.redirecting.explanation: Write the final address, where the redirect ends, as the canonical.
idx4.redirecting.why: A canonical should name the final address; a redirecting one makes engines follow an extra step and weakens the signal.
steps: Write the address the redirect ends at as canonical
Fix the template or plugin that writes the old address
idx4.redirecting.verify: Open the canonical address from the page source with curl; it should answer with the page, without a redirect.

idx4.same.title: Confirm canonicals to same-content pages
idx4.same.finding: Pages are canonicalized to a same-content address
idx4.same.explanation: This is normal consolidation; confirm it is intended, and otherwise make the page its own canonical.
idx4.same.why: Pointing same-content pages at one canonical joins their signals. If the target is wrong, the wanted page may not show.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Check that the target is the right page
If not, fix the page's canonical
idx4.same.verify: In Search Console URL Inspection, the canonical Google chose should match the declared one.

idx4.variant.title: Write canonicals with the site's own https address
idx4.variant.finding: Canonical points at the http or www version of the site
idx4.variant.explanation: Write the canonical with the address the page is served at: its https scheme and its own host.
idx4.variant.why: A canonical on the http or www version names an address the site does not serve the page at, so engines get a second, weaker address.
steps: Find the template or plugin that writes the canonical
Make it write the site's https scheme and its own host
Check the platform's primary domain setting
idx4.variant.verify: The canonical address in the page source should have the same scheme and host as the browser's address bar.

idx5.bad_share.title: Remove failing and noindexed pages from the sitemap
idx5.bad_share.finding: The sitemap lists failing or noindexed addresses
idx5.bad_share.explanation: Keep only addresses that load cleanly and are indexable in the sitemap; fix or remove the rest.
idx5.bad_share.why: A sitemap that lists missing or blocked pages is trusted less, and crawlers spend visits on pages that cannot be used.
steps: Find the failing or noindexed addresses in the sitemap
Fix the pages that should stay
Take the others out of the sitemap
idx5.bad_share.verify: Open the sitemap addresses with curl; each should answer successfully and carry no noindex.

idx5.corrupt.title: Repair sitemap addresses with broken characters
idx5.corrupt.finding: Sitemap addresses contain spaces or broken encoding
idx5.corrupt.explanation: Compare these addresses with their original record in the CMS and repair only the ones that are clearly corrupted.
idx5.corrupt.why: An address with a space or a broken character differs from the page's real address, so crawlers cannot reach the page through the sitemap.
steps: Compare the broken addresses with their records in the CMS
Rewrite the clearly corrupted ones with the right characters
Fix the encoding in the plugin or template that writes the sitemap
idx5.corrupt.verify: Open the sitemap file in a browser; no address should contain a space or a broken character.

idx5.drafts.title: Remove test pages from the index and the sitemap
idx5.drafts.finding: Draft or test pages are indexable and in the sitemap
idx5.drafts.explanation: Remove draft or test pages or add noindex to them, and take them out of the sitemap.
idx5.drafts.why: A draft or test page in the sitemap is offered to engines as a page of the site, and may be shown or quoted in place of a finished one.
steps: Confirm the pages are tests or drafts
Remove them, or add noindex if they must stay
Take them out of the sitemap
idx5.drafts.verify: The sitemap file should no longer list these addresses; opened, they should carry noindex or return a not-found response.

idx5.failed_files.title: Fix or remove the sitemap files that do not load
idx5.failed_files.finding: Some sitemap files could not be loaded
idx5.failed_files.explanation: Make every sitemap file named in the sitemap index or robots.txt load, or remove the ones that do not.
idx5.failed_files.why: The named sitemap file did not load when requested. Its pages can then be found only through links and other sitemaps.
steps: Open the sitemap files that do not load
Fix them or remove them from the index and robots.txt
idx5.failed_files.verify: In the Search Console Sitemaps report, each file should show the status Success.

idx5.future.title: Fix sitemap lastmod values set in the future
idx5.future.finding: Sitemap lastmod values are in the future
idx5.future.explanation: Take lastmod values from each page's real last edit date and remove dates set in the future.
idx5.future.why: A change date in the future is an obvious error, and makes the sitemap's other dates less believable.
steps: Find the future lastmod values in the sitemap
Check the time zone and date source of the plugin or template that writes them
Take lastmod from each page's last edit date
idx5.future.verify: Open the sitemap file; no lastmod value should show a date later than today.

idx5.identical.title: Replace identical lastmod dates with real ones
idx5.identical.finding: All sitemap lastmod values are identical
idx5.identical.explanation: Take each page's lastmod from its own last edit date, or leave lastmod out if that is not possible.
idx5.identical.why: When every page claims the same change date, the dates carry no information and engines stop using them to decide what to re-read.
steps: Take lastmod from each page's last edit date
If that is not possible, consider leaving lastmod out
idx5.identical.verify: Open the sitemap file; lastmod values should show the pages' different edit dates.

Shopify: Shopify writes the sitemap itself; lastmod cannot be edited by hand
lastmod is when the product or collection was last updated
Find the apps that update everything at once (stock, price, translation)
Stop needless bulk saves; change the app's setting if needed

idx5.malformed.title: Fix wrongly written sitemap addresses
idx5.malformed.finding: Sitemap addresses have a “?” or a space in place of a letter
idx5.malformed.explanation: Write each address exactly as the page's real address, replacing broken letters with the right characters.
idx5.malformed.why: An address with a “?” where a letter should be leads to another address, so the page is not found through the sitemap.
steps: Compare the wrong addresses with the pages' real addresses
Fix the character encoding in the tool that writes the sitemap
Rebuild the sitemap and submit it again
idx5.malformed.verify: Open the sitemap file; each address should match the address the page opens at in a browser.

idx5.no_image_sitemap.title: List the main images in the sitemap
idx5.no_image_sitemap.explanation: List the pages' main images in the sitemap or in a separate image sitemap.
idx5.no_image_sitemap.why: Image entries in the sitemap help engines find and index the images of a site with many, including ones loaded late or by a script.
steps: Add <image:image> entries for each page's main images
Or add an image sitemap and name it in robots.txt
idx5.no_image_sitemap.verify: Open the sitemap file; page entries should contain <image:image> items.

idx5.no_video_sitemap.title: List the videos in a video sitemap
idx5.no_video_sitemap.explanation: List the videos on the pages in a video sitemap, with their title, description and thumbnail.
idx5.no_video_sitemap.why: A video sitemap tells engines where each video is, what it is about and which thumbnail to show, so videos can appear in video results.
steps: Add <video:video> entries: title, description, thumbnail
Or add a video sitemap and name it in robots.txt
idx5.no_video_sitemap.verify: Open the sitemap file; entries for pages with a video should contain <video:video> items.

idx5.none.title: Publish an XML sitemap
idx5.none.finding: No usable XML sitemap was found
idx5.none.explanation: Publish an XML sitemap that lists the pages you want indexed, and name it in robots.txt.
idx5.none.why: A sitemap is the list of pages you want found. On a larger site, pages that are not well linked are found late or not at all without one.
steps: Create an XML sitemap that lists the indexable pages
Add its address to robots.txt with a Sitemap: line
Submit the sitemap in Search Console
idx5.none.verify: In the Search Console Sitemaps report, the sitemap should show the status Success.

idx5.not_encoded.title: Consider percent-encoding sitemap addresses
idx5.not_encoded.finding: Sitemap addresses have letters that are not percent-encoded
idx5.not_encoded.explanation: This is a note, not an error; if the generator supports it, have special letters written percent-encoded.
idx5.not_encoded.why: Addresses are meant to be written with letters outside A to Z percent-encoded. Most crawlers read both forms.
steps: Check the sitemap generator's percent-encoding setting
If it is supported, have special letters written encoded
idx5.not_encoded.verify: Open the sitemap file; accented letters should appear in percent-encoded form.

idx5.not_live.title: Remove pages that are not live from the sitemap
idx5.not_live.finding: Some sitemap addresses are not live, indexable pages
idx5.not_live.explanation: Keep only pages that open directly and are indexable in the sitemap; remove redirecting, empty or noindexed ones.
idx5.not_live.why: A sitemap that lists missing, redirected, empty or noindexed pages is trusted less, and crawlers spend visits on pages that cannot be used.
steps: Find failing, redirecting, empty or noindexed addresses in the sitemap
Replace redirecting addresses with their final address
Take pages that will not stay out of the sitemap
idx5.not_live.verify: Open the sitemap addresses with curl; each should answer successfully without a redirect and carry no noindex.

idx5.not_live.beside.title: Remove pages that are not live from the sitemap
idx5.not_live.beside.finding: Besides the empty pages, more sitemap addresses are not live
idx5.not_live.beside.explanation: Keep only pages that open directly and are indexable in the sitemap; remove redirecting, empty or noindexed ones.
idx5.not_live.beside.why: A sitemap that lists missing, redirected, empty or noindexed pages is trusted less, and crawlers spend visits on pages that cannot be used.
steps: Find failing, redirecting, empty or noindexed addresses in the sitemap
Replace redirecting addresses with their final address
Take pages that will not stay out of the sitemap
Fix the empty pages with the steps given for them in this report
idx5.not_live.beside.verify: Open the sitemap addresses with curl; each should answer successfully without a redirect and carry no noindex.

idx5.not_live.idx1.title: Remove pages that are not live from the sitemap
idx5.not_live.idx1.finding: Sitemap addresses are not live; some are empty pages
idx5.not_live.idx1.explanation: Keep only pages that open directly and are indexable in the sitemap; remove redirecting, empty or noindexed ones.
idx5.not_live.idx1.why: A sitemap that lists missing, redirected, empty or noindexed pages is trusted less, and crawlers spend visits on pages that cannot be used.
steps: Find failing, redirecting, empty or noindexed addresses in the sitemap
Replace redirecting addresses with their final address
Take pages that will not stay out of the sitemap
Fix the empty pages with the steps given for them in this report
idx5.not_live.idx1.verify: Open the sitemap addresses with curl; each should answer successfully without a redirect and carry no noindex.

idx5.not_live.sampled.title: Remove pages that are not live from the sitemap
idx5.not_live.sampled.finding: Some of the checked sitemap addresses are not live
idx5.not_live.sampled.explanation: Keep only pages that open directly and are indexable in the sitemap; remove redirecting, empty or noindexed ones.
idx5.not_live.sampled.why: A sitemap that lists missing, redirected, empty or noindexed pages is trusted less, and crawlers spend visits on pages that cannot be used.
steps: Find failing, redirecting, empty or noindexed addresses in the sitemap
Replace redirecting addresses with their final address
Take pages that will not stay out of the sitemap
Review the remaining unchecked addresses the same way
idx5.not_live.sampled.verify: Open the sitemap addresses with curl; each should answer successfully without a redirect and carry no noindex.

idx5.not_live.sampled.beside.title: Remove pages that are not live from the sitemap
idx5.not_live.sampled.beside.finding: Besides the empty pages, more checked addresses are not live
idx5.not_live.sampled.beside.explanation: Keep only pages that open directly and are indexable in the sitemap; remove redirecting, empty or noindexed ones.
idx5.not_live.sampled.beside.why: A sitemap that lists missing, redirected, empty or noindexed pages is trusted less, and crawlers spend visits on pages that cannot be used.
steps: Find failing, redirecting, empty or noindexed addresses in the sitemap
Replace redirecting addresses with their final address
Take pages that will not stay out of the sitemap

idx5.not_live.sampled.beside.verify: Open the sitemap addresses with curl; each should answer successfully without a redirect and carry no noindex.

idx5.not_live.sampled.idx1.title: Remove pages that are not live from the sitemap
idx5.not_live.sampled.idx1.finding: Some checked addresses are not live; some are empty pages
idx5.not_live.sampled.idx1.explanation: Keep only pages that open directly and are indexable in the sitemap; remove redirecting, empty or noindexed ones.
idx5.not_live.sampled.idx1.why: A sitemap that lists missing, redirected, empty or noindexed pages is trusted less, and crawlers spend visits on pages that cannot be used.
steps: Find failing, redirecting, empty or noindexed addresses in the sitemap
Replace redirecting addresses with their final address
Take pages that will not stay out of the sitemap
Fix the empty pages with the steps given for them in this report
idx5.not_live.sampled.idx1.verify: Open the sitemap addresses with curl; each should answer successfully without a redirect and carry no noindex.

idx5.query_unassessed.title: Check sitemap addresses with a question mark
idx5.query_unassessed.explanation: Compare these addresses with their original record to see whether each is an intended query or a broken letter.
idx5.query_unassessed.why: A question mark can start a valid query, or stand in for a broken letter. If it is broken, the page is not found through the sitemap.
steps: Compare the addresses with their original records
If the question mark replaces a broken letter, fix the address
If it is an intended query, leave it as it is
idx5.query_unassessed.verify: Open the addresses in a browser; each should show the expected page.

idx5.stamped.title: Take sitemap lastmod dates from the real edit dates
idx5.stamped.finding: The sitemap gives nearly every address the same lastmod
idx5.stamped.explanation: Take lastmod values from each page's real edit date, not from a stamp the sitemap generator adds.
idx5.stamped.why: Dates stamped by the generator, not by real changes, tell engines nothing about which pages changed.
steps: Take lastmod from each page's last edit date
If that is not possible, consider leaving lastmod out
idx5.stamped.verify: In the sitemap, each address's lastmod value should show the date that page last changed.

idx6.alias_links.title: Link to each page's canonical address
idx6.alias_links.finding: Internal links point at duplicate, non-canonical addresses
idx6.alias_links.explanation: Point internal links at each page's canonical address instead of a duplicate address.
idx6.alias_links.why: A link to a duplicate address sends crawlers to a page they then fold into another: visits are spent twice and the canonical page gets its links second-hand.
steps: Find the template that writes the alias links
Make it write the canonical address instead
idx6.alias_links.verify: In the page source, internal links should point at each page's canonical address.

Shopify: Find the template that writes the alias links
Make it write the canonical address instead
