idx6.broken.title: Fix or remove links to addresses that return an error
idx6.broken.finding: Links lead to an address that returns an error
idx6.broken.explanation: Point links to an address that returns an error at a working page, or remove them.
idx6.broken.why: A broken link sends visitors and crawlers to nothing.
steps: Open each page that carries the link
Point the link at a working page or remove it
idx6.broken.verify: Open a page that carries the link and click it; a working page should open.

idx6.cf_email.title: Make the e-mail address readable without a script
idx6.cf_email.finding: Cloudflare e-mail obfuscation hides the address behind JavaScript
idx6.cf_email.explanation: If the address is meant to be read and quoted, turn off e-mail obfuscation in Cloudflare or wrap it in email_off comments.
idx6.cf_email.why: Cloudflare swaps the address for a placeholder that a script turns back into the address. A crawler or assistant that runs no script sees no address.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
If not, turn off Email Address Obfuscation in Cloudflare Scrape Shield
Or wrap the address in email_off comments
idx6.cf_email.verify: Open the page's HTML source; the e-mail address should appear as plain text.

idx6.external_cycle.title: Check external links that loop
idx6.external_cycle.finding: Some external links showed a redirect cycle
idx6.external_cycle.explanation: Open these external addresses in a browser to confirm the cycle, and update or remove the link if it persists.
idx6.external_cycle.why: A redirect cycle keeps visitors and crawlers from reaching the target. The result may differ in another browser or with cookies.
steps: Open the external addresses in a normal browser
If the cycle persists, replace the link with a working address
If there is no suitable address, remove the link
idx6.external_cycle.verify: Click the link; the target site should open a page without looping.

idx6.external_gone.title: Update links to removed pages on other sites
idx6.external_gone.finding: External links lead to removed pages
idx6.external_gone.explanation: Point external links that return a not-found or gone response at a current source, or remove them.
idx6.external_gone.why: A link to a page another site has removed sends visitors to an error page and tells engines the page is not kept up to date.
steps: Open the pages that carry the links
Find the new address of the target content and update the link
If there is no new address, remove the link
idx6.external_gone.verify: Click the links; each should open a working page on the other site.

idx6.other_site.title: Fix internal-looking links that go to another site
idx6.other_site.finding: Some links open a path of this site on another site
idx6.other_site.explanation: Point these links at the same path on this site, and fix the menu or template that writes the other domain.
idx6.other_site.why: A menu or footer link that looks internal but leaves the site sends visitors and crawlers away from the page they expected.
steps: Confirm whether the link is meant to go to the other site
Find the menu, footer or template that writes the link
Remove the other domain and write this site's address
idx6.other_site.verify: Click the links; visitors should stay on the same domain and the page on this site should open.

idx6.other_site_dead.title: Fix internal-looking links that go to another site
idx6.other_site_dead.finding: Internal-looking links lead to an error on another site
idx6.other_site_dead.explanation: Point these links at the same path on this site, and fix the menu or template that writes the other domain.
idx6.other_site_dead.why: A link that looks internal but goes to another site's missing page sends visitors and crawlers to an error.
steps: Confirm whether the link is meant to go to the other site
Find the menu, footer or template that writes the link
Remove the other domain and write this site's address
idx6.other_site_dead.verify: Click the links; visitors should stay on the same domain and the page on this site should open.

idx6.other_site_unchecked.title: Fix internal-looking links that go to another site
idx6.other_site_unchecked.finding: Internal-looking links go to another site; the target was not checked
idx6.other_site_unchecked.explanation: Point these links at the same path on this site, and fix the menu or template that writes the other domain.
idx6.other_site_unchecked.why: A link that looks internal leaves the site; whether the other page exists could not be checked.
steps: Confirm whether the link is meant to go to the other site
Find the menu, footer or template that writes the link
Remove the other domain and write this site's address
idx6.other_site_unchecked.verify: Click the links; visitors should stay on the same domain and the page on this site should open.

idx6.tracking.title: Remove tracking parameters from internal links
idx6.tracking.explanation: Write internal links with the page's clean address, without tracking parameters such as utm.
idx6.tracking.why: Internal links with tracking parameters create a second address for the same page, which splits its signals and wastes crawler visits.
steps: Find utm and similar parameters on internal links
Write the links with the clean address
idx6.tracking.verify: Internal links in the page source should carry no utm or similar parameters.

idx7.deep.title: Link important deep pages from closer pages
idx7.deep.finding: Some pages are many clicks from the homepage
idx7.deep.explanation: Link important deep pages from menus, categories or hub pages to shorten their path from the homepage.
idx7.deep.why: Pages many clicks deep are crawled later and less often, and are treated as less important.
steps: Decide which of the deep pages matter
Link them from menus, categories or hub pages
Shorten long pagination chains with category links
idx7.deep.verify: Click your way from the homepage to an important page; the path should be shorter than before.

idx7.orphan.title: Link to pages that are only in the sitemap
idx7.orphan.finding: Some pages are reachable only from the sitemap
idx7.orphan.explanation: Link the pages that will stay live from related pages, and remove the ones that are no longer needed.
idx7.orphan.why: A page that nothing links to is found only through the sitemap, and engines treat pages nobody links to as less important.
steps: Confirm the pages should stay live
If so, link to them from related pages
idx7.orphan.verify: The source of related pages should show internal links to these pages.

idx7.pagination_unlinked.title: Link each list page to the next one
idx7.pagination_unlinked.finding: List pages do not link to their next page with <a href>
idx7.pagination_unlinked.explanation: Write a real <a href> link to the next page in each list page's HTML.
idx7.pagination_unlinked.why: Crawlers follow <a href> links, not buttons or scrolling. Without a link to the next page, items listed only there are found late or not at all.
steps: Add <a href> links to the next pages in the list's HTML
Keep "load more" or scrolling beside the links
idx7.pagination_unlinked.verify: The list page's source should show an <a href> link carrying the next page's address.

idx7.product_no_category.title: Link each product back to its category
idx7.product_no_category.finding: Product pages have no link to a category
idx7.product_no_category.explanation: Add a breadcrumb trail or a link to the product's category on each product page.
idx7.product_no_category.why: A link from each product back to its category tells engines how the catalogue is organised and passes visits on to the category.
steps: Add a breadcrumb trail with links to the product template
Or link to the product's main category in its content
Mark the trail up with BreadcrumbList
idx7.product_no_category.verify: The product page source should show a category link, and Rich Results Test should show BreadcrumbList.

idx8.copies.title: Merge or differentiate pages that copy each other
idx8.copies.finding: Some indexable pages copy each other
idx8.copies.explanation: Merge copies that serve the same purpose, permanently redirecting the old addresses, and make the rest distinct.
idx8.copies.why: Pages that copy each other compete with each other, and an engine picks one per group to show, which may not be the one you want.
steps: Compare what each copied page is for
Merge pages that serve the same purpose
Rewrite the ones that stay so each is distinct
idx8.copies.verify: Open the pages in a group; each should show its own text or permanently redirect to one address.

idx8.identical.title: Gather pages with the same text at one address
idx8.identical.finding: Some indexable pages show identical text
idx8.identical.explanation: Choose one address and permanently redirect the others to it, or point their canonical at it.
idx8.identical.why: When several addresses show the same content, engines pick one to show, and it may not be the one you want.
steps: Confirm the pages with the same text serve the same purpose
Choose one as the main address
Permanently redirect the others to it, or point their canonical at it
idx8.identical.verify: Open the other addresses; they should redirect to the main one or name it as canonical in their source.

idx8.location_template.title: Give each place page content of its own
idx8.location_template.finding: Place pages differ mostly by the place name
idx8.location_template.explanation: Add information only true of each place to its page, or keep one list page and remove the copies.
idx8.location_template.why: Many pages that repeat one text with only the place name changed can be treated as doorway pages, and none gives a reason to be shown.
steps: Add information that is only true of each place
Such as hours, menu, address, team or reviews
Or keep one list page and remove the copies
idx8.location_template.verify: Open the place pages side by side; each should show information specific to that place.

idx8.merged.title: Merge or differentiate pages that copy each other
idx8.merged.finding: Some indexable pages copy each other
idx8.merged.explanation: Merge copies that serve the same purpose, permanently redirecting the old addresses, and make the rest distinct.
idx8.merged.why: Pages that copy each other compete with each other, and an engine picks one per group to show, which may not be the one you want.
steps: Compare what each copied page is for
Merge pages that serve the same purpose
Rewrite the ones that stay so each is distinct
idx8.merged.verify: Open the pages in a group; each should show its own text or permanently redirect to one address.

idx8.near.title: Differentiate pages with nearly identical content
idx8.near.finding: Some indexable pages have nearly identical main content
idx8.near.explanation: Merge near-identical pages with a permanent redirect from the old address, or give each one distinct content.
idx8.near.why: Pages that say almost the same thing compete with each other, and an engine may show only one of them.
steps: Compare what the near-identical pages are for
Merge them or give each distinct content
idx8.near.verify: Open the pages side by side; each should show distinct main content or redirect to one address.

idx8.title.title: Write a distinct title for pages that share one
idx8.title.finding: Some indexable pages share the same title
idx8.title.explanation: Write a unique <title> on each page that tells its topic apart from the others.
idx8.title.why: Pages with the same title look like the same page in search results, so engines and visitors cannot tell them apart.
steps: List the pages that share the title
Write a <title> for each that names its own topic
Fix the template that writes a fixed title so it uses the page name
idx8.title.verify: The <title> tags in the pages' source should differ from each other.

idx8.two_addresses.title: Choose one address for pages reachable at two
idx8.two_addresses.finding: Some pages open at two different addresses
idx8.two_addresses.explanation: Choose one address and permanently redirect the other to it.
idx8.two_addresses.why: A page at two addresses gets its links and signals split between them, and engines choose which one to show.
steps: Confirm both addresses show the same page
Keep one and permanently redirect the other to it
idx8.two_addresses.verify: Open the second address with curl; it should permanently redirect to the main address.

idx9.canonical.title: Align Google's chosen canonical with yours
idx9.canonical.finding: Google chose a different canonical than the page declares
idx9.canonical.explanation: Make the canonical tag, internal links and sitemap name the same address, and strengthen the content if needed.
idx9.canonical.why: Google treats the canonical as a hint. If it chooses another address, that address is indexed and shown instead of the one you declared.
steps: Review the canonical Google chose in Search Console
Make the canonical tag, internal links and sitemap name the same address
Then request indexing in URL Inspection
idx9.canonical.verify: In Search Console URL Inspection, the Google-selected canonical should match the one you declared.

idx9.no_rule.title: Review key pages Google has not indexed
idx9.no_rule.finding: Google reports key pages as not indexed
idx9.no_rule.explanation: Read each page's coverage state in Search Console and decide on the fix from the reason Google gives.
idx9.no_rule.why: This is Google's own record of whether the page is in its index. A page that is not indexed cannot appear in Google's results or AI answers.
steps: Read the page's coverage state in Search Console URL Inspection
Fix the page based on the reason Google gives
Then request indexing
idx9.no_rule.verify: In Search Console URL Inspection, the page should be shown as on Google and indexable in the live test.

idx9.noindex.title: Fix key pages excluded by noindex
idx9.noindex.finding: Google excludes key pages because of noindex
idx9.noindex.explanation: If noindex is not intended, remove it from the page's HTML and HTTP header, then request indexing.
idx9.noindex.why: This is Google's own record of whether the page is in its index. A page that is not indexed cannot appear in Google's results or AI answers.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
If not, remove noindex from the HTML and the X-Robots-Tag header
Request indexing in Search Console
idx9.noindex.verify: In Search Console URL Inspection, the page should be shown as on Google and indexable in the live test.

idx9.robots.title: Lift the robots.txt block from key pages
idx9.robots.finding: Google reports key pages blocked by robots.txt
idx9.robots.explanation: If the block is not intended, remove or narrow the matching Disallow rule in robots.txt.
idx9.robots.why: This is Google's own record of whether the page is in its index. A page that is not indexed cannot appear in Google's results or AI answers.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
If not, remove or narrow the matching Disallow rule in robots.txt
Request indexing in Search Console
idx9.robots.verify: The Search Console robots.txt report and URL Inspection should show the page as not blocked.

idx9.state.title: Resolve the indexing issue Google reports
idx9.state.finding: Google reports key pages as not indexed
idx9.state.explanation: Resolve the reason Google gives, such as noindex, thin content or the canonical, then request indexing.
idx9.state.why: This is Google's own record of whether the page is in its index. A page that is not indexed cannot appear in Google's results or AI answers.
steps: Read each page's coverage state in Search Console
Remove noindex, strengthen the content or fix the canonical, as the reason requires
Request indexing in Search Console
idx9.state.verify: In Search Console URL Inspection, the page should be shown as on Google and indexable in the live test.

judgment.empty.repeated.title: Fix pages that answer with an empty body
judgment.empty.repeated.finding: Some addresses keep answering with an empty body
judgment.empty.repeated.explanation: Find the source of the empty answer in the server and cache logs, and make the page answer with its content.
judgment.empty.repeated.why: A page that answers empty has nothing to read, so search engines and AI crawlers cannot index or quote it.
steps: Open the addresses in a browser and with curl
Check the server or cache log
Fix what makes them answer empty
judgment.empty.repeated.verify: Open the address with curl; the response body should contain the page's HTML.

judgment.empty.single.title: Confirm and fix the empty responses
judgment.empty.single.explanation: Open the addresses again to confirm whether the empty answer persists, and check the server log if it does.
judgment.empty.single.why: One empty answer does not mean a lasting problem. If it persists, crawlers find nothing to read on the page.
steps: Open the addresses again to confirm the empty answer
If it persists, check the server log
judgment.empty.single.verify: Open the address with curl a few times; each response body should contain the page's HTML.

judgment.external.mixed.title: Check external links with mixed results
judgment.external.mixed.finding: Some external addresses gave different results per request
judgment.external.mixed.explanation: Open these external addresses in a normal browser to see whether they work, and update the link if one is broken.
judgment.external.mixed.why: Some sites answer automated requests differently. Only a manual check shows whether a link is really broken.
steps: Open the external addresses in a normal browser
Replace the ones that do not work, or remove them
judgment.external.mixed.verify: Click the links; each should open the expected page on the other site.

judgment.generic.title: Review generic link texts such as 'click here'
judgment.generic.explanation: Read links such as 'read more' in their context, and where needed replace them with text that names the target.
judgment.generic.why: Link text tells crawlers and assistive technology what the target is. Generic text does not say that without its context.
steps: Read links such as 'read more' in their context
Where needed, write text that names the target
judgment.generic.verify: In the page source, link texts or accessible names should name the target page.

judgment.generic.identity.title: Review generic link texts such as 'click here'
judgment.generic.identity.explanation: Read links such as 'read more' in their context, and where needed replace them with text that names the target.
judgment.generic.identity.why: Link text tells crawlers and assistive technology what the target is. Generic text does not say that without its context.
steps: Read links such as 'read more' in their context
Where needed, write text that names the target
judgment.generic.identity.verify: In the page source, link texts or accessible names should name the target page.

judgment.head.title: Check external links that reported an error
judgment.head.finding: Some external addresses gave an error to a quick check
judgment.head.explanation: Open these external addresses in a normal browser to see whether the page really opens, and update broken links.
judgment.head.why: An error on a quick check does not show on its own that the target page was removed. Whether it opens needs a separate check.
steps: Open the external addresses in a normal browser
Replace the ones that do not work, or remove them
judgment.head.verify: Click the links; each should open the expected page on the other site.

judgment.heading.home.title: Fill the homepage's empty main heading
judgment.heading.home.finding: The homepage's main heading is empty
judgment.heading.home.explanation: Write meaningful text in the homepage's main heading that says what the site offers.
judgment.heading.home.why: An empty main heading does not state the page's topic, so search and AI answer engines must infer it from other signals.
steps: Write what the site offers into the empty main heading
If the template leaves the main heading empty, fill it there
judgment.heading.home.verify: In the homepage source, the main heading tag should contain meaningful text.

judgment.heading.pages.title: Write meaningful text in empty main headings
judgment.heading.pages.finding: Some pages have an empty main heading
judgment.heading.pages.explanation: Write meaningful text in each page's main heading that names the page's topic.
judgment.heading.pages.why: An empty main heading does not state the page's topic, so search and AI answer engines must infer it from other signals.
steps: Fill the empty main heading with text that names the topic
Fix the template that leaves the heading empty
judgment.heading.pages.verify: In the pages' source, the main heading tag should contain meaningful text.

judgment.sitemap.title: Review the sitemap addresses that do not work
judgment.sitemap.explanation: Review each address's response and whether it should be indexed, then fix it or take it out of the sitemap.
judgment.sitemap.why: A sitemap that lists failing addresses is trusted less. Before changing it, find out why each address fails.
steps: Find the failing addresses in the sitemap
Fix them or take them out of the sitemap
judgment.sitemap.verify: Open the sitemap addresses with curl; each should answer successfully and be indexable.

judgment.sitemap.overlap.title: Review the sitemap addresses that do not work
judgment.sitemap.overlap.finding: Some sitemap addresses need review; some are empty pages
judgment.sitemap.overlap.explanation: Review each address's response and whether it should be indexed, then fix it or take it out of the sitemap.
judgment.sitemap.overlap.why: A sitemap that lists failing addresses is trusted less. Before changing it, find out why each address fails.
steps: Find the failing addresses in the sitemap
Fix them or take them out of the sitemap
judgment.sitemap.overlap.verify: Open the sitemap addresses with curl; each should answer successfully and be indexable.

prf1.home_ttfb.title: Speed up the homepage's first response
prf1.home_ttfb.finding: The homepage is slow to start answering
prf1.home_ttfb.explanation: Cache the homepage HTML, or speed up what the server does before it answers.
prf1.home_ttfb.why: The homepage is the page every visitor and crawler reaches first. When it is slow to start answering, everything that follows starts late.
steps: Ask the platform for a page cache on the homepage
Or cache the homepage HTML at the CDN
Otherwise find what the server does before answering
prf1.home_ttfb.verify: Open the homepage with curl a few times; the time to first byte should be shorter than before.

prf1.no_hsts.title: Add the Strict-Transport-Security header to https answers
prf1.no_hsts.finding: The homepage sends no Strict-Transport-Security header
prf1.no_hsts.explanation: Add the Strict-Transport-Security header to https answers from the web server, the application or the CDN.
prf1.no_hsts.why: This header tells browsers to use https only. It is a security setting; no answer engine documents using it.
steps: Turn on Strict-Transport-Security in the server, application or CDN settings
Give the header a long max-age
Add includeSubDomains if every subdomain supports https
prf1.no_hsts.verify: Open the homepage with curl; the response headers should include Strict-Transport-Security.

prf1.not_cached.title: Cache page HTML at the CDN
prf1.not_cached.finding: Page HTML is not cached at the CDN
prf1.not_cached.explanation: Cache the HTML of pages that look the same to everyone at the CDN, and keep personal pages out of it.
prf1.not_cached.why: When the CDN does not keep a copy of the HTML, every visitor and crawler waits for the origin server, often the slowest part of the answer.
steps: Set a cache rule for HTML at the CDN
Keep personal pages such as cart and account out of the rule
Check for Cache-Control or cookie headers that prevent caching
prf1.not_cached.verify: Open the page with curl twice; the CDN's cache header should show HIT on the second answer.

prf1.security_headers.title: Add baseline security headers to the homepage
prf1.security_headers.finding: The homepage answers without some baseline security headers
prf1.security_headers.explanation: Add the missing security headers to answers from the web server, the application or the CDN.
prf1.security_headers.why: Security headers protect visitors from injected scripts, framing and leaks of the address they came from. They are not a search signal.
steps: List the missing headers from the report's details
Add headers such as Content-Security-Policy or X-Frame-Options at the server or CDN
Check that the site still works after the change
prf1.security_headers.verify: Open the homepage with curl; the added security headers should appear in the response headers.

prf1.slow.title: Speed up the slow pages
prf1.slow.finding: Some pages return their HTML slowly
prf1.slow.explanation: Find why the slow pages answer late, then cache them or speed up the slow queries.
prf1.slow.why: A slow server makes crawlers read fewer pages per visit, and some give up before the page arrives.
steps: Find why the slow pages answer late
Cache them or speed up the slow queries
prf1.slow.verify: Open the pages with curl a few times; the HTML should arrive faster than before.

prf1.timeouts.title: Fix pages that time out now and then
prf1.timeouts.finding: Some addresses time out on some attempts
prf1.timeouts.explanation: Find the cause of the timeouts in the server or CDN logs, and make the pages answer every request.
prf1.timeouts.why: A page that sometimes does not answer is sometimes missing when a crawler visits.
steps: Retry the addresses that time out
Find the cause of the delay in the server or CDN log
Speed up slow queries or cache the page
prf1.timeouts.verify: Open the addresses with curl a few times; every request should get an answer without a timeout.

prf2.rate.title: Find the source of failing requests across the site
prf2.rate.finding: A noticeable share of requests failed during the audit
prf2.rate.explanation: Investigate the origin server's stability, and match the times of the failures with server and CDN logs.
prf2.rate.why: When a noticeable share of all requests fail, the site as a whole looks unreliable to crawlers.
steps: Find the error responses in the server and CDN logs
Note the times and addresses where errors cluster
Check capacity, rate limit and firewall settings
prf2.rate.verify: In the Search Console Crawl stats report, check the share of server error responses; it should be low.

prf2.some.title: Find why some requests fail intermittently
prf2.some.finding: Some addresses fail now and then
prf2.some.explanation: Retry the addresses that fail now and then, and find the cause in the server or CDN log.
prf2.some.why: Pages that fail now and then are sometimes missing when a crawler visits, and crawlers come back less often to unreliable sites.
steps: Retry the addresses that fail now and then
Find the cause in the server or CDN log
prf2.some.verify: Open the addresses with curl a few times; every attempt should get a successful answer.

prf3.poor.title: Improve the Core Web Vitals
prf3.poor.finding: Real-user measurements put some metrics in the poor range
prf3.poor.explanation: Improve the metric in the poor range, whether loading, interaction or layout shift, for real visitors.
prf3.poor.why: Core Web Vitals describe how fast the page feels to real visitors, measured by Google from real visits. The effect on AI answers is indirect.
steps: Find the poor metric and its causes in PageSpeed Insights
Shrink large images and defer blocking scripts
Reserve space for elements that shift the layout
prf3.poor.verify: The Search Console Core Web Vitals report should show the addresses out of the poor range.

rnd1.maybe.title: Check suspected client-side rendering in a browser
rnd1.maybe.finding: Page may be rendered on the client
rnd1.maybe.explanation: Open these pages in a browser, check whether the main content is in the raw HTML, and render it on the server if it is missing.
rnd1.maybe.why: The HTML looks like an empty shell that a script fills in. If so, crawlers that do not run JavaScript see no content.
steps: Open one of the pages with JavaScript turned off
Check whether the main text is in the page source
If it is missing, render the main content on the server
rnd1.maybe.verify: Open the page source in a browser; the main text should be there before any JavaScript runs.

rnd1.missing.title: Render the main content on the server
rnd1.missing.finding: Main content missing from the raw HTML
rnd1.missing.explanation: Render the main content on the server or prerender the pages, so the text is in the first HTML response.
rnd1.missing.why: Many AI crawlers do not run JavaScript. Content that appears only after scripts run is invisible to them.
steps: Render the main content on the server (SSR)
Or prerender the pages
rnd1.missing.verify: Open the page source in a browser; the main text should be there before any JavaScript runs.
rnd1.missing.summary: Content not rendered on the server

rnd1.partial.title: Put the missing content into the server's HTML
rnd1.partial.finding: Part of the content missing from the raw HTML
rnd1.partial.explanation: Find the sections that only JavaScript adds and put them into the HTML the server sends.
rnd1.partial.why: Part of the page appears only after JavaScript runs. Crawlers that do not run it see an incomplete page.
steps: Find the missing sections from the quoted text
Render those sections on the server
rnd1.partial.verify: Open the page source in a browser; the text of the sections quoted in the report should be there.

rnd2.after_js.title: Put critical facts into the server's HTML
rnd2.after_js.finding: Critical facts appear only after JavaScript
rnd2.after_js.explanation: Put critical facts such as prices into the visible text the server sends, not only into JavaScript.
rnd2.after_js.why: Key facts such as prices should be in the page the server sends. Crawlers that do not run JavaScript never see them.
steps: List the critical facts that only JavaScript adds
Output them as visible text on the server
rnd2.after_js.verify: Open the page source in a browser; each critical fact should be there as visible text.

rnd2.candidates.title: Put headings and prices into the server's HTML
rnd2.candidates.finding: Headings and prices appear only after JavaScript
rnd2.candidates.explanation: Once you confirm they matter, move headings and prices that appear only after JavaScript into the server's HTML.
rnd2.candidates.why: Headings and prices that appear only after scripts run are missing for crawlers that do not run them.
steps: Find headings and prices that only JavaScript adds
Put them into the server's HTML
rnd2.candidates.verify: Open the page source in a browser; these headings and prices should be there before JavaScript runs.

rnd2.markup_only.title: Show critical facts as visible text
rnd2.markup_only.finding: Critical facts exist only in markup
rnd2.markup_only.explanation: Show the critical facts that sit only in script data or attributes as visible text on the page as well.
rnd2.markup_only.why: Script data and attributes are not visible text. Crawlers and AI engines that read the text may miss the fact.
steps: Find the critical facts that live only in markup
Show them as visible text on the page
rnd2.markup_only.verify: Open the page in a browser; each critical fact should be readable in its visible text.

rnd2.not_found.title: Update critical facts that were not found
rnd2.not_found.finding: Critical fact not found on its page
rnd2.not_found.explanation: Check the page, then update either its text or the declared critical fact.
rnd2.not_found.why: If a declared fact is missing, its wording changed or it was removed. Engines cannot quote a fact the page does not contain.
steps: Check how the fact is worded on the page
If the declared fact is outdated, update it
If the page lost the fact, add it back
rnd2.not_found.verify: Open the page in a browser; the declared fact should appear there in the same wording.

rnd3.maybe.title: Check content behind interaction in a browser
rnd3.maybe.finding: Content may be hidden behind interaction
rnd3.maybe.explanation: Open one of the pages in a browser and check whether tab and accordion content is in the first HTML.
rnd3.maybe.why: The HTML suggests content behind tabs, accordions or 'load more'. Crawlers do not click, so that content may go unread.
steps: Open one of the pages in a browser
Check whether tab and accordion text is in the page source
If not, put that content in the first HTML; it can stay collapsed
rnd3.maybe.verify: In the page source, the text behind tabs, accordions and 'load more' should appear.

rnd3.revealed.title: Show the hidden content without a click
rnd3.revealed.finding: Content appears only after a click or scroll
rnd3.revealed.explanation: Put the content that opens on a click or scroll into the first HTML; it can stay visually collapsed.
rnd3.revealed.why: Crawlers do not click or scroll. Text that appears only after a visitor does is not read.
steps: Find the content that opens only on a click
Show the important parts openly on the page
rnd3.revealed.verify: Open the page source in a browser; the text of the sections that open on a click should be there.

rnd4.banner.title: Write alt text for banner images
rnd4.banner.finding: Banner images have no alt text
rnd4.banner.explanation: If the banner images contain text, put that text in the HTML or in descriptive alt text.
rnd4.banner.why: Text inside a picture cannot be read by engines. If the banners contain words, those words are missing from the page for an engine.
steps: Put the banner's words into its alt text
Also give important text outside the image
rnd4.banner.verify: In the page source, each banner image's alt attribute should carry the words shown in the image.

rnd4.canvas.title: Add a text equivalent for canvas content
rnd4.canvas.finding: Canvas content has no text equivalent
rnd4.canvas.explanation: Add a text equivalent, such as a table, an aria-label or fallback content, for what the canvas shows.
rnd4.canvas.why: A canvas draws pixels, not text. A chart or diagram drawn there cannot be read by an engine unless the page also says it in text.
steps: Find out what the canvas shows
Add it to the page as a table, text or aria-label
rnd4.canvas.verify: In the page source, what the canvas shows should also be there as text.

rnd4.iframe.title: Review the content in embedded frames
rnd4.iframe.finding: Page embeds content in an iframe
rnd4.iframe.explanation: Review what each embedded frame holds, and add equivalent page text only if essential facts are found only there.
rnd4.iframe.why: An iframe embeds a separate document. That alone is not a problem, but engines may not tie essential facts inside it to the page.
steps: Find out what each iframe shows
If essential facts are only in the frame, add them as page text
rnd4.iframe.verify: Open the page in a browser; essential facts should be readable outside the frame too.

rnd4.layout_canvas.title: Confirm the site-wide canvas is decoration
rnd4.layout_canvas.finding: Site layout has a canvas with no text equivalent
rnd4.layout_canvas.explanation: If the canvas only decorates, mark it with aria-hidden; if it shows something readers need, add a text equivalent.
rnd4.layout_canvas.why: A canvas draws pixels, not text. One on every page is usually a background effect, but what it shows still needs a check.
steps: Confirm what the canvas draws
If it is decoration, add aria-hidden="true"
If it shows information, add a text equivalent
rnd4.layout_canvas.verify: In the page source, the canvas should carry aria-hidden or come with a text equivalent.

rnd4.unnamed.title: Give embedded frames an accessible name
rnd4.unnamed.finding: Embedded frames have no accessible name
rnd4.unnamed.explanation: Give each embedded frame a title attribute that says what it holds.
rnd4.unnamed.why: A frame with no name does not tell screen reader users what it holds. This is an accessibility matter, not proof of a search problem.
steps: Give each <iframe> a title that says what it holds
Fix frames that come from the template once there
rnd4.unnamed.verify: In the page source, each <iframe> tag should have a meaningful title attribute.

rnd5.account_login.title: Check that account pages stay out of the index
rnd5.account_login.finding: Account pages send visitors to sign in
rnd5.account_login.explanation: This is expected; only check that account, cart and checkout pages are not in the sitemap or the index.
rnd5.account_login.why: A page that belongs to one signed-in customer has nothing for a crawler to read. It is enough that it stays out of search results.
steps: Confirm these are account, cart or checkout pages
Check that they are not listed in the sitemap
rnd5.account_login.verify: In the sitemap and in the Pages report in Search Console, these addresses should not show as indexed.

rnd5.in_place.title: Show the wall as an overlay on the content
rnd5.in_place.finding: Page serves a wall instead of the content
rnd5.in_place.explanation: Put the content in the HTML and show the consent, login, age or location wall as an overlay on top of it.
rnd5.in_place.why: Crawlers cannot pass walls. If the HTML holds only the wall, a crawler reads the wall, not the content behind it.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Put the content into the HTML the server sends
Turn the wall into an overlay on top of the content
rnd5.in_place.verify: Open the page source in a private window with no cookies; the content text should appear along with the wall.

rnd5.paywall.title: Mark paywalled content with structured data
rnd5.paywall.explanation: Add structured data with isAccessibleForFree and hasPart, so engines can tell a paywall from cloaking.
rnd5.paywall.why: Structured data tells engines plainly that a paywall is there. An unmarked paywall can look like showing crawlers and visitors different content.
steps: Confirm the page really has a paywall
Add isAccessibleForFree: false to its structured data
Mark the gated section with hasPart
rnd5.paywall.verify: In the Rich Results Test, the page's structured data should show the isAccessibleForFree value.

rnd5.redirect.title: Stop redirecting cookie-less visitors to a wall
rnd5.redirect.finding: Cookie-less visitors are redirected to a wall
rnd5.redirect.explanation: Serve the content to visitors without cookies, and show the wall as an overlay instead of redirecting.
rnd5.redirect.why: Crawlers carry no cookies and cannot pass walls. A redirected crawler never sees the content, only the login or consent page.
steps: Confirm whether this is intended
Remove the redirect and serve the content to cookie-less visitors
Show the consent or age question as an overlay on the content
rnd5.redirect.verify: Open the address in a private window with no cookies; the page should open with its own content, without a redirect.

rnd6.home_large.title: Slim down the homepage HTML
rnd6.home_large.explanation: Move inline JSON, CSS, scripts and SVG out of the homepage HTML into files, and remove unused blocks.
rnd6.home_large.why: A heavy homepage is slower for every visit and leaves less of a crawler's budget for the content itself.
steps: Move inline JSON, CSS and scripts into files
Remove unused blocks and templates from the theme
If the theme is locked, ask the platform
rnd6.home_large.verify: In the browser's network tab or PageSpeed Insights, the homepage HTML should look compact and light.

rnd6.home_large_fc.title: Slim down the homepage HTML
rnd6.home_large_fc.explanation: Check the homepage's raw HTML size, and if it is heavy, move inline code and data into separate files.
rnd6.home_large_fc.why: This was measured on the HTML after scripts ran and is not comparable with raw size. A heavy homepage is slower for every visit.
steps: Measure the homepage's raw HTML size in the browser's network tab
Move inline JSON, CSS and scripts into separate files
Remove unused blocks and templates from the theme
rnd6.home_large_fc.verify: In the browser's network tab, the homepage document's transferred size should look light.

rnd6.large.title: Slim down the oversized HTML pages
rnd6.large.explanation: Move inline JSON, CSS and SVG into separate files and remove embedded code the page does not use.

steps: Move inline JSON, CSS and SVG into separate files
Remove embedded code the page does not use

rnd6.large_fc.title: Slim down the oversized HTML pages
rnd6.large_fc.explanation: Check these pages' raw HTML size, and if it is heavy, move inline JSON, CSS and SVG into separate files.

Move inline JSON, CSS and SVG into separate files
Remove embedded code the page does not use
rnd6.large_fc.verify: In the browser's network tab, these pages' HTML document should look light.

rnd6.late.title: Bring the main content closer to the top of the HTML

rnd6.late.explanation: Move large inline scripts, styles and data after the main content or into separate files.

rnd6.late_fc.title: Bring the main content closer to the top of the HTML
rnd6.late_fc.finding: Main content starts late in rendered HTML
rnd6.late_fc.explanation: Check where the main content starts in the raw HTML, and move large inline code before it into separate files if needed.
rnd6.late_fc.why: This was measured on the HTML after scripts ran and is not comparable with raw size. A crawler that reads only the start may miss the content.
steps: Check where the main content starts in the page source
Move the large inline code before it into separate files
rnd6.late_fc.verify: In the page source, the main text should appear soon after the menus, before large code blocks.

rnd7.no_region.title: Wrap the main content in <main> or <article>
rnd7.no_region.explanation: Wrap the page's main content in a <main> or <article> element.
rnd7.no_region.why: These elements mark plainly where the main content is. Without them, engines have to separate the content using other hints.
steps: Find the element that wraps the main content in the template
Turn that element into <main> or <article>
rnd7.no_region.verify: In the page source, the main content should sit inside a single <main> or <article> element.

rnd7.share.title: Review the balance of main content and repeated areas
rnd7.share.finding: Main content is a small share of page text
rnd7.share.explanation: Inspect the measured main content area and the repeated menus, and adjust the boundaries or the text where needed.
rnd7.share.why: When most text sits in menus and footers, engines may struggle to find the page's own part. A low share alone does not prove a fault.
steps: Check that the main content area is marked up correctly
Review the repeated menu and footer text
Strengthen the page's own text where needed
rnd7.share.verify: In the page source, the page's own text inside <main> should clearly outweigh the menu and footer.

shared.block_links_no_text.title: Name the links in the shared block

steps: Give the block's links text or an aria-label
Fix it once in the template

shared.heading_jump.title: Fix the heading level in the shared area

shared.heading_jump.explanation: Bring the shared heading's level into the page's heading order, and fix it in the template.

Fix it once in the template

Fix it once in the template
shared.heading_jump_varied.verify: In the page source, the shared heading should sit just one level below the heading before it.

shared.image_no_alt.title: Write alt text for the shared image
shared.image_no_alt.finding: Shared image has no alt text
shared.image_no_alt.explanation: Write alt text that says what the shared image shows, or leave alt empty if it is only decoration.
shared.image_no_alt.why: Alt text is how an engine, and a screen reader, knows what an image shows. A gap in a shared area repeats on every page.

If it carries information, write what it shows in its alt text
Fix it once in the template
shared.image_no_alt.verify: In the page source, the image's tag should have a meaningful alt, or a deliberately empty one.

shared.link_generic.title: Write descriptive text for the shared link
shared.link_generic.finding: Shared link has only generic text
shared.link_generic.explanation: Replace generic link text such as 'read more' with text that names the topic of the target page.
shared.link_generic.why: Link text tells engines what the linked page is about. 'Click here' tells them nothing.
steps: Write link text that names the target page's topic
Fix it once in the template
shared.link_generic.verify: In the page source, the shared link's text should name the topic of the page it leads to.

shared.link_no_address.title: Give the shared link an address
shared.link_no_address.explanation: Give the shared link the address of the page it opens, or make it a button if it only opens a panel.

If it only opens a panel, make it a <button>

shared.link_no_text.title: Name the shared link that has no text

steps: Add an aria-label to the shared link
Fix it once in the template; every page follows
shared.link_no_text.verify: In the page source, the link's visible text or aria-label should say where it leads.

shared.link_no_text_pattern.title: Name the template links that have no text
shared.link_no_text_pattern.explanation: Give the template's links to the same kind of address visible text or an aria-label.
shared.link_no_text_pattern.why: A link with no text gives engines, and screen readers, no idea where it leads.
steps: Find the template part that outputs these links
Add visible text or an aria-label to the link
If it wraps an image, give the image alt text
shared.link_no_text_pattern.verify: In the page source, each of these links should have visible text or an aria-label.

shared.links_no_address.title: Give the shared links an address
shared.links_no_address.explanation: Give the shared links the address of the page they open, and turn those that only open a panel into buttons.
shared.links_no_address.why: A crawler follows addresses, not clicks. A link with '#' or a script in place of an address gives it nothing to follow, even when it works for a visitor.
steps: Give the links the address of the page they open
If they only open a panel, make them <button>
Fix it once in the template
shared.links_no_address.verify: In the page source, each link's href should be a real page address, or the element should be a <button>.

str1.generic.title: Replace generic titles with the page's topic
str1.generic.explanation: Replace generic titles such as 'Home' with a <title> that names the page's topic and the site name.
str1.generic.why: A title such as 'Home' or only the site name says nothing about what the page is about.

Put the site name at the end of the title
str1.generic.verify: In the page source's <title> tag and the browser tab, the page's topic should be readable.

str1.no_title.title: Write a title for pages that have none
str1.no_title.explanation: Write a <title> that names each page's topic, and fill the template field that leaves the title empty.
str1.no_title.why: The title is the name an engine shows for the page. Without one, the engine makes one up.
steps: Write a <title> that names each page's topic
Fill the template field that leaves the title empty
str1.no_title.verify: In the page source, each page should have a filled <title> tag specific to its topic.

str1.same_start.title: Put what sets each page apart at the start of its title
str1.same_start.finding: Titles begin with the same words
str1.same_start.explanation: Put the topic that sets the page apart at the start of the title, and the brand name or tagline at the end.
str1.same_start.why: Repeated starts can hide the page's topic when a title is cut short. Display width varies; there is no fixed character limit.
steps: List the titles that begin with the same words
Move the page's own topic to the start of each title
Move the shared tagline or brand name to the end
str1.same_start.verify: In the page source's <title> tags, the first words should differ from page to page.

str1.shared.title: Give pages that share a title their own title
str1.shared.finding: Title is shared by several pages
str1.shared.explanation: Write each page that shares a <title> its own title that sets it apart from the others.
str1.shared.why: When many pages share a title, engines and readers cannot tell which page covers what.
steps: List the pages that share a <title>
Give each a title that says what sets it apart
str1.shared.verify: In the page sources, each indexable page should have a <title> tag of its own.

str10.empty_tag.title: Fill the empty meta tags
str10.empty_tag.explanation: Fill the empty preview tag with a value that fits the page, or remove the tag altogether.
str10.empty_tag.why: An empty preview tag can leave a gap when the page is shared or shown as a source. Check the real preview on each channel too.
steps: Find the template field that outputs the empty tag
Fill the field with a value that fits the page
If no value can be given, remove the tag
str10.empty_tag.verify: In the page source, the meta tag's content value should be filled.

str10.icon.title: Use a real image as the share image
str10.icon.finding: Share image is the site icon
str10.icon.explanation: Put a large, wide image that represents the page in og:image, instead of the site icon.
str10.icon.why: The share image is what appears when the page is shared or shown as a source. A tiny site icon is blurred or left out of the preview.

Pick a large, wide image that represents the page
Point og:image at that image
str10.icon.verify: In Facebook Sharing Debugger, the page preview should show a wide image instead of the site icon.

str10.no_description.title: Write the missing meta descriptions
str10.no_description.explanation: Write each important page a meta description of its own that sums up its content.
str10.no_description.why: The meta description is the summary that search results and shares may show. Without one, the engine picks a snippet from the page text.
steps: List the important pages with no meta description
Write each a description that sums up its content
Check that the template outputs the description field
str10.no_description.verify: In the page source, each important page should have a filled meta description tag.

str10.no_tag.title: Add the missing preview tags

Add that tag to the template with the page's own value
str10.no_tag.verify: In Facebook Sharing Debugger, the page preview should show the right title, description and image.

str10.no_twitter.verify: In the page source, the twitter:card tag should appear, and a link shared on X should open as a card with an image.

str10.og_image_dead.title: Replace share images that return an error

Replace it with a working image
str10.og_image_dead.verify: Open the og:image address in a browser; the image should open without an error.

str10.small.title: Use a larger share image

steps: List the pages with a small share image
Prepare a large, wide image for each
Point og:image at the new image
str10.small.verify: In Facebook Sharing Debugger, the image in the page preview should look sharp and large.

str10.thumb.title: Bring the share image up to large-card size
str10.thumb.finding: Share image shows as a small thumbnail
str10.thumb.explanation: For the large card, put a wide image in og:image, in the size the platforms recommend.
str10.thumb.why: When the image is not large enough for the large card, the big networks show it as a small thumbnail beside the text.
steps: List the pages with a thumbnail-size share image
Prepare a wide image in large-card size
Point og:image at the new image
str10.thumb.verify: In Facebook Sharing Debugger, the page should show as a card with a large, wide image.

str11.two_values.title: Remove the conflicting structured data values

str12.headings.title: Translate the section headings in another language

str13.raw_only.finding: Template markers only in the raw HTML

str14.generic.title: Make generic link texts descriptive

str15.empty_collections.title: Fill, merge or hide empty collections

str18.no_brand.title: Add the brand name to the homepage title

str19.lead_nowhere.title: Fix links that lead nowhere

str19.no_target.title: Give links an address or make them buttons

str19.no_target.explanation: Give links that open a page that page's address, and turn elements that only run a script into buttons.
str19.no_target.why: A crawler follows addresses, not clicks. A link with '#' or a script in place of an address gives it nothing to follow, even when it works for a visitor.
steps: Give links that open a page that page's address
Turn elements that only run a script into <button>
str19.no_target.verify: In the page source, each link's href should be a real address, or the element should be a <button>.

str2.empty_h1.title: Write the page topic into empty main headings
str2.empty_h1.explanation: Write the page's topic into the empty main heading, and fill the template field if the template leaves it empty.

If the template leaves the main heading empty, fill it there

str2.hidden_h1.title: Make the main heading visible where it is hidden

str2.home_hidden_h1.title: Make the homepage's main heading visible

str2.home_no_h1.title: Add one main heading to the homepage

str2.home_outline.verify: In the homepage source, each section should start with a subheading tag.

str2.many_h1.title: Keep one main heading per page
