str2.many_h1.verify: In the page source, only one main heading tag should appear.

str2.no_h1.title: Add one main heading to pages that have none
str2.no_h1.explanation: Add one main heading that names each page's topic, and define it once in the template.
str2.no_h1.why: The main heading tells engines what the page is about. Without it they rely on weaker hints.
steps: Add one main heading that names the page's topic
Define the main heading once in the template
str2.no_h1.verify: In the page source, one main heading tag that names the page's topic should appear.

str2.no_subheadings.title: Add section headings to long pages
str2.no_subheadings.explanation: Add meaningful subheadings to the sections of long pages; none are needed where tables and lists already split the text.
str2.no_subheadings.why: Subheadings divide a long page into passages an engine can quote one at a time.
steps: Add meaningful subheadings to long sections
Tables and lists that already split the text need none
str2.no_subheadings.verify: In the page source, the long text should be split into sections by meaningful subheading tags.

str20.media.title: Write the video's message on the page as text
str20.media.finding: Message is only in video or animation
str20.media.explanation: Write the video's key points on the page as text: who you are, what you offer and for whom.
str20.media.why: Crawlers read text; they do not watch video or run animation. A message that exists only in a video is, for an engine, not on the page.
steps: Sum up the video's main message in a few sentences
Add the summary or a transcript to the page as text
str20.media.verify: In the page source, the video's main message should appear as readable text.

str21.missing.title: Add the missing basic page
str21.missing.finding: A basic page was not found
str21.missing.explanation: Add the missing About, Contact, product or service, or FAQ page, or make the existing one say what it is.
str21.missing.why: Engines and visitors look for who is behind a site, what it offers and how to reach it. A topic with no page has nothing to quote.
steps: Note which page kind the report lists as missing
If it does not exist, create it and link it from the menu and footer
If it exists, name it in its address, title or main heading
str21.missing.verify: The site's menu or footer should link to the page, and the page should open.

str22.link_lists.title: Add your own text to news pages
str22.link_lists.finding: News pages are mostly links to other sites
str22.link_lists.explanation: Write a short summary in your own words next to each news or press link.
str22.link_lists.why: A news page that only links out sends engines elsewhere for the story. The site then has nothing of its own to be quoted for it.
steps: Review the entries on the news or press page
Write a short summary of what each entry says
Publish your own article on the site for important news
str22.link_lists.verify: On the news page, each link should have a summary written by the site next to it.

str23.listed.title: Add JobPosting structured data to open positions
str23.listed.finding: Jobs are listed with no JobPosting data
str23.listed.explanation: Give each open position its own page and add JobPosting structured data to it.
str23.listed.why: JobPosting markup is how search engines recognise a page as an open position. Google requires it to show a job in its job listings.
steps: Create a separate page for each open position
Add JobPosting with title, description, date posted and location
Remove closed positions from the page and the markup
str23.listed.verify: In the Rich Results Test, each job page should show a valid JobPosting.

str23.pages.title: Add JobPosting to job pages
str23.pages.finding: Job pages have no JobPosting data
str23.pages.explanation: Add JobPosting structured data with title, description, date posted and location to each job page.
str23.pages.why: JobPosting markup is how search engines recognise a page as an open position. Google requires it to show a job in its job listings.
steps: Add JobPosting to the job page template
Fill in title, description, date posted, employer and location
Add validThrough to closed jobs, or remove the page
str23.pages.verify: In the Rich Results Test, each job page should show a valid JobPosting.

str3.article_no_author.title: Name the author of each article
str3.article_no_author.explanation: Show the author's name on each article, link it to an author page and add it to the Article markup.
str3.article_no_author.why: A named author with a page of their own is one of the signals engines use to judge who stands behind advice and how far to trust it.
steps: Show the author's name on each article
Link it to an author page
Add author (a Person) to the Article markup
str3.article_no_author.verify: The article should show an author name, and the Rich Results Test should show author in the Article markup.

str3.crumb_no_list.title: Add BreadcrumbList to the breadcrumb trail
str3.crumb_no_list.explanation: Describe the breadcrumb trail the page shows with BreadcrumbList, one ListItem per step, in order.
str3.crumb_no_list.why: BreadcrumbList tells engines where a page sits in the site in a form machines read. Search results may show this trail instead of the address.
steps: Find the breadcrumb trail the template shows
Add a ListItem with a name and address for each step
Keep the steps in the order shown on the page
str3.crumb_no_list.verify: The Rich Results Test should show a BreadcrumbList whose steps match the trail on the page.

str3.dangling_id.title: Fix @id references that point nowhere
str3.dangling_id.explanation: Define the referenced node with a type (usually on the homepage), or reference an @id that exists.
str3.dangling_id.why: A reference to something that is defined nowhere leaves that part of the structured data empty.
steps: Find the @id values named in the evidence
Define that node, with its type, on the homepage
Or replace the reference with an @id that exists
str3.dangling_id.verify: In the Schema Markup Validator, every @id reference should lead to a node with a type.

str3.expected_type.title: Add the structured data type each page kind expects
str3.expected_type.finding: Pages lack the type their kind expects
str3.expected_type.explanation: Add the expected type to each page kind: Article to articles, Product to products, Offer to price pages.
str3.expected_type.why: Structured data states what a page is (a product, an article) in a form machines read directly.
steps: Add Article to articles, Product to products, Offer to price pages
Do not add these types to list or pagination pages
str3.expected_type.verify: In the Rich Results Test, each page should show the structured data type for its kind.

str3.invalid_values.title: Correct the structured data values
str3.invalid_values.finding: Structured data values cannot be read
str3.invalid_values.explanation: Write rating, price and currency values in a form Google reads: plain numbers and standard codes.
str3.invalid_values.why: A rating or price Google cannot read as a number or code is dropped, so the item loses what it was marked up to show.
steps: Use a period as the decimal separator
Remove spaces around property names
Write the currency in capitals (TRY)
str3.invalid_values.verify: The Rich Results Test should show no warnings about value formats.

str3.maybe_product.title: Check whether single-price pages are products
str3.maybe_product.finding: A single-price page may be a product page
str3.maybe_product.explanation: If these pages sell one product, add Product structured data with an Offer; if not, nothing is needed.
str3.maybe_product.why: A page that shows one price may sell one product. If it does, Product structured data says so to the engines that read it.
steps: Check whether each page sells one product
If it does, add Product structured data with an Offer
If it is a service or menu page, leave it as it is
str3.maybe_product.verify: In the Rich Results Test, pages that sell a product should show Product and Offer.

str3.no_organization.title: Add Organization structured data to the homepage
str3.no_organization.finding: The homepage has no Organization data
str3.no_organization.explanation: Add an Organization block with name, address, logo and official profiles (sameAs) to the homepage.
str3.no_organization.why: Organization markup on the homepage tells engines who is behind the site: name, logo and official profiles.
steps: Add an Organization JSON-LD block to the homepage
Fill in name, url and logo
Add the official social profiles as sameAs
str3.no_organization.verify: In the Schema Markup Validator, the homepage should show an Organization with a name and logo.

str3.organization_broken.title: Fix the homepage's Organization block
str3.organization_broken.finding: The Organization block does not parse
str3.organization_broken.explanation: Find the value where the parser stops in the Organization block and fix the character that breaks it.
str3.organization_broken.why: A block that does not parse is ignored whole, so the Organization it describes is not read at all.
steps: Find the value where the parser stops (see evidence)
Remove or escape the line break in that value
Do not add a second Organization block
str3.organization_broken.verify: In the Schema Markup Validator, the homepage's Organization block should read without errors.

str3.organization_gaps.title: Complete the Organization structured data
str3.organization_gaps.explanation: Add the missing logo and official profile links (sameAs) to the homepage's Organization block.
str3.organization_gaps.why: A logo and profile links let engines tie the site to the brand's other official pages.
steps: Note which fields the report lists as missing
Put the logo's full address in the logo field
Add the official profiles to the sameAs list
str3.organization_gaps.verify: In the Schema Markup Validator, the Organization should show logo and sameAs.

str3.product_no_identifier.title: Add GTIN or MPN to the Product markup
str3.product_no_identifier.finding: Product markup has no GTIN or MPN
str3.product_no_identifier.explanation: Add each product's GTIN (barcode), or its MPN when there is none, and the brand to the Product markup.
str3.product_no_identifier.why: A GTIN or MPN lets Google match the product to the same item elsewhere, which its shopping results and merchant listings rely on.
steps: Add the GTIN (barcode), or the MPN when there is none
Add the brand too
str3.product_no_identifier.verify: In the Rich Results Test, the Product markup should show a gtin or mpn field.

Shopify: Add the GTIN (barcode), or the MPN when there is none
Add the brand too
On Shopify: fill each variant's barcode field

str3.qa_no_faqpage.title: Mark up question-and-answer content with FAQPage
str3.qa_no_faqpage.finding: Q&A shown, no FAQPage structured data
str3.qa_no_faqpage.explanation: Describe the questions and answers the page shows as Question and Answer items in FAQPage.
str3.qa_no_faqpage.why: FAQPage states questions and answers in a form machines read directly. Google shows FAQ rich results only for official health and government sites.
steps: Add each question shown on the page as a Question
Put its answer in acceptedAnswer, as written on the page
Do not mark up questions the page does not show
str3.qa_no_faqpage.verify: In the Schema Markup Validator, FAQPage and the page's questions should show without errors.

str3.required.title: Add the required structured data properties
str3.required.explanation: Add the properties Google requires for each structured data type, as listed missing in the evidence.
str3.required.why: Google ignores structured data that lacks the properties it requires for that type.
steps: List the missing properties by type from the evidence
Fill them with the real values shown on the page
Do not invent a value; drop the type if there is none
str3.required.verify: The Rich Results Test should show no errors about required properties.

str3.type_clash.title: Give each @id one type
str3.type_clash.finding: An @id has different types in different places
str3.type_clash.explanation: Use one @id per entity and give it the same type everywhere.
str3.type_clash.why: When one @id is given different types, engines cannot tell what it is, and what they know about the entity is split.
steps: Find the @id values with different types in the evidence
Choose the right type for each
Use that type for the @id on every page
str3.type_clash.verify: In the Schema Markup Validator, each @id should show the same type on every page.

str3.unparsed.title: Fix JSON-LD that does not parse
str3.unparsed.explanation: Find where the parser stops in the broken JSON-LD block and fix the syntax error.
str3.unparsed.why: Structured data that does not parse is ignored entirely, as if it were not there.
steps: Find where the parser stops (see evidence)
Fix the missing comma, quote or unescaped line break
Update the template or plugin that writes the block
str3.unparsed.verify: In the Schema Markup Validator, the block should read without errors.

str3.url_differs.title: Match the structured data URL to the canonical
str3.url_differs.finding: Structured data URL differs from the canonical
str3.url_differs.explanation: Make the markup's url the page's canonical URL, so the entity and the page point at one address.
str3.url_differs.why: When the markup's address and the canonical differ, engines may tie the entity and the page to different addresses.
steps: Find the differing url values in the evidence
Replace each with the address in the page's canonical tag
Check where the template takes the address from
str3.url_differs.verify: In the page source, the markup's url and the canonical tag should show the same address.

str3.url_error.title: Fix broken URLs in structured data
str3.url_error.finding: A structured data URL returns an error
str3.url_error.explanation: Point the markup's url at the page's live canonical URL.
str3.url_error.why: An address in structured data that leads to an error points engines at nothing.
steps: Find the url values that return an error in the evidence
Replace them with the page's canonical URL
Check that the template does not write old or wrong addresses
str3.url_error.verify: In a browser, the address in the markup should open the page itself.

str3.video_default.title: Fill in the VideoObject with real details
str3.video_default.finding: VideoObject looks like an unfilled default
str3.video_default.explanation: Fill in the VideoObject's name, description, thumbnail and upload date with the video's real details.
str3.video_default.why: A placeholder name or date tells engines nothing true about the video and can make the markup look unreliable.
steps: Find the placeholder name, description or date
Replace them with the video's real details
Remove the markup from a video with no details
str3.video_default.verify: In the Rich Results Test, the VideoObject should show a real name, thumbnail and date.

str4.differs.title: Match structured data to what the page shows
str4.differs.finding: Structured data disagrees with the page
str4.differs.explanation: Generate the structured data value (price, stock, date, name) from the same source as the value shown.
str4.differs.why: When structured data disagrees with the visible page, an engine may quote the wrong value or trust neither.
steps: Find the differing field and values in the evidence
Confirm which value is right
Generate the markup from the same data as the page
str4.differs.verify: The value in the Rich Results Test should match the value shown on the page.

str4.not_shown.title: Show the marked-up information on the page
str4.not_shown.explanation: Show each structured data value on the page too, or remove values the page does not show from the markup.
str4.not_shown.why: Google asks sites not to mark up things readers cannot see. A value in the markup that is not on the page may be ignored, or may be out of date.
steps: Find the field the page does not show in the evidence
If the value is right, show it on the page
If not, or if it is old, remove it from the markup
str4.not_shown.verify: The page should show the markup's value where a reader can see it.

str4.other_state.title: Check that the page can show the other marked-up prices
str4.other_state.finding: Markup lists prices not shown when read
str4.other_state.explanation: Check that each price behind a switch, such as monthly or yearly, can be selected on the page.
str4.other_state.why: The markup lists prices the page did not show when read, usually the other side of a monthly/yearly switch. That is not a conflict.
steps: Open each price switch on the page (monthly, yearly)
Check that each marked-up price appears under one option
Remove from the markup any price no option shows
str4.other_state.verify: When the page's price options are opened, each marked-up price should appear in one of them.

str4.price_unclear.title: Show the marked-up price clearly on the page
str4.price_unclear.finding: Markup price not shown or not distinguishable
str4.price_unclear.explanation: Show the marked-up price clearly on the page and make clear which of the page's prices is this offer.
str4.price_unclear.why: Google asks sites not to mark up things readers cannot see. A price in the markup that is not on the page may be ignored, or may be out of date.
steps: Compare the markup price with the prices on the page
Show the right price clearly next to the product
Remove an old or wrong price from the markup
str4.price_unclear.verify: On the page, the marked-up price should appear clearly next to the product name.

str5.id_names.title: Give the brand @id the same name on every page
str5.id_names.explanation: Use one official brand name in every block that carries the same brand @id.
str5.id_names.why: When one @id carries different names, engines cannot tell which is the brand's real name.
steps: Find the @id values with different names in the evidence
Choose the official brand name
Write that name in every block with that @id
str5.id_names.verify: In the Schema Markup Validator, each @id should show the same name on every page.

str5.names.title: Use one name for the brand across the site
str5.names.finding: The brand is named in different ways
str5.names.explanation: Choose one brand name and use it in titles, og:site_name and Organization across the site.
str5.names.why: A consistent name helps engines recognise the brand as one entity across the site.
steps: Choose the one brand name the site uses
Use it in titles, og:site_name and Organization
str5.names.verify: In the page source, titles, og:site_name and Organization should show the same brand name.

str5.og_site_name.title: Set og:site_name to the site's name only
str5.og_site_name.explanation: Put only the site's name in og:site_name and keep the page's own title in og:title.
str5.og_site_name.why: og:site_name is where a page says which site it belongs to. A page title in it gives every page a different site name.
steps: Put only the site's name in og:site_name
Keep the page's own title in og:title
str5.og_site_name.verify: In the page source, og:site_name should show the same site name on every page.

str5.same_as.title: Fix dead sameAs links
str5.same_as.explanation: Replace dead profile links with the current profile address, or remove them from the sameAs list.
str5.same_as.why: Profile links tell engines which social and directory pages belong to the brand. Dead ones weaken that.
steps: Find the profile links that return a not-found response
If a profile moved, use its new address
If a profile was closed, remove it from the sameAs list
str5.same_as.verify: In a browser, each profile address in the sameAs list should open.

str6.apart.title: Make the page's dates agree
str6.apart.explanation: Generate the date shown, the structured data date and the sitemap lastmod from the same source.
str6.apart.why: When a page's dates disagree, engines cannot tell how fresh it is.
steps: Find the differing dates in the evidence
Confirm the real published and updated dates
Generate every date field from the same source
str6.apart.verify: The page, its structured data and the sitemap should show the same updated date.

str6.future.title: Fix future dates
str6.future.finding: The page carries a future date
str6.future.explanation: Replace future published or updated values with the real date.
str6.future.why: A date in the future is an obvious error and makes the page's other dates less believable.
steps: Find the field with the future date in the evidence
Replace it with the real published or updated date
Check the time zone and format in the template that writes it
str6.future.verify: The page and its structured data should show no date after today.

str6.no_date.title: Add published and updated dates to articles
str6.no_date.finding: Articles show no published or updated date
str6.no_date.explanation: Show the published and updated dates on each article and add datePublished and dateModified to the Article markup.
str6.no_date.why: Dates tell engines how fresh an article is. Without one, it may be treated as old.
steps: Show the published date in the article template
Show the updated date too when the content changes
Add datePublished and dateModified to the Article markup
str6.no_date.verify: The article should show a date, and the Rich Results Test should show datePublished.

str6.stamped.title: Compare the automatic dates with edit records
str6.stamped.explanation: Compare these dates with the real edit records, and change how dates are generated only if they are wrong.
str6.stamped.why: The date pattern needs comparison with actual edit records. Same-day values alone do not prove incorrect dates.
steps: Compare a few pages' dates with their edit records
Check whether the date changes with real edits
If it is wrong, update the date only when the content changes
str6.stamped.verify: In the content system's edit records, the last change should match the date on the page.

str7.alt_missing.title: Write alt text for images that carry information
str7.alt_missing.finding: Images lack alt text or have an empty one
str7.alt_missing.explanation: Give each informative image a short alt text that says what it shows.
str7.alt_missing.why: Alt text is how an engine, and a screen reader, knows what an image shows.
steps: List the images with missing or empty alt text
Give the informative ones alt text that says what they show
Leave an empty alt on decorative images
str7.alt_missing.verify: In the page source, each informative image should have a filled alt value.

str7.alt_split.title: Write alt text for images that carry information
str7.alt_split.finding: Images have no alt text or an empty alt
str7.alt_split.explanation: Give the informative images among those with missing or empty alt text an alt text that says what they show.
str7.alt_split.why: Alt text is how an engine, and a screen reader, knows what an image shows.
steps: Pick out the empty-alt images that carry information
Give those alt text that says what they show
str7.alt_split.verify: In the page source, each informative image should have a filled alt value.

str7.broken.title: Fix images that do not load
str7.broken.finding: Some image files do not load
str7.broken.explanation: Restore each image file that does not load, or correct its address in the page.
str7.broken.why: An image that does not load shows visitors an empty space, and engines cannot index it.
steps: Find the image addresses that do not load in the evidence
Restore the file or correct the address
Remove images that are no longer used from the page
str7.broken.verify: In a browser, each image address should open and show the image.

str7.format_references.title: Check the image formats actually delivered
str7.format_references.finding: Markup does not show the delivered format
str7.format_references.explanation: Compare the image format the server actually sends, its file size and its quality.
str7.format_references.why: WebP or AVIF references in markup do not prove the delivered format. Savings are not guaranteed; compare size and quality first.
steps: Look up a few images' delivered format in the browser's developer tools
Compare file size and quality with a WebP or AVIF version
Serve images in a modern format where it saves bytes
str7.format_references.verify: The Network tab of the browser's developer tools should show each image's delivered format and size.

str7.format_unassessed.title: Assess the image formats delivered
str7.format_unassessed.finding: WebP or AVIF delivery was not assessed
str7.format_unassessed.explanation: Compare the delivered format, file size and quality on sample images, so the next audit can read this too.
str7.format_unassessed.why: Markup observations do not prove the delivered image format. Savings are not guaranteed; compare size and quality first.
steps: Look up a few images' delivered format in the browser's developer tools
Compare file size and quality with a WebP or AVIF version
Serve images in a modern format where it saves bytes
str7.format_unassessed.verify: The Network tab of the browser's developer tools should show each image's delivered format and size.

str7.formats.title: Consider serving images in a modern format
str7.formats.finding: Some images are not offered in a modern format
str7.formats.explanation: After comparing size and quality, serve content images that use older formats as WebP or AVIF.
str7.formats.why: Markup references do not prove the delivered image format. Savings are not guaranteed; compare size and quality first.
steps: Identify content images served in older formats
Compare size and quality with a WebP or AVIF version
Serve images in a modern format where it saves bytes
str7.formats.verify: The Network tab of the browser's developer tools should show content images as WebP or AVIF.

str7.heavy.title: Resize and compress the heavy images
str7.heavy.explanation: Resize heavy images to the largest size they are shown at and compress them, or serve them as WebP/AVIF.
str7.heavy.why: Heavy images slow the page down; on mobile in particular the main content appears late and Core Web Vitals suffer.
steps: Resize each image to the largest size it is shown at
Compress it or serve WebP/AVIF
Replace the file at the same address
str7.heavy.verify: PageSpeed Insights should show no suggestions about image size.

str7.mime.title: Serve images in the format their file name says
str7.mime.finding: Image format does not match the file name
str7.mime.explanation: Convert the image to the format its file name says, or rename the file to match its real format.
str7.mime.why: The browser still shows the image, but the mismatch usually means a photo was never converted to JPEG or WebP and stays heavier than needed.
steps: Find the mismatched images in the evidence
Convert each to JPEG or WebP and upload it again
Update the address in the page to the new file
str7.mime.verify: In the browser's developer tools, the image's content type should match the format in its file name.

str7.no_alt.title: Add an alt attribute to the other images
str7.no_alt.finding: Some images have no alt attribute
str7.no_alt.explanation: Give every image an alt attribute: a description for informative ones, an empty one for decorative ones.
str7.no_alt.why: Without an alt attribute, screen readers may read out the file name, and engines cannot tell what the image shows.
steps: Find the images with no alt attribute
Describe what the informative ones show
Give decorative images an empty alt attribute
str7.no_alt.verify: In the page source, every image tag should have an alt attribute.

str7.placeholder.title: Replace placeholder alt texts
str7.placeholder.explanation: Replace placeholder alt texts with text that says what the image really shows.
str7.placeholder.why: A filename or generic label may not describe an informative image. Its actual purpose, equivalent text and decorative intent need review.
steps: Describe what each informative image shows
Keep an empty alt on decorative images
Do not generate descriptions from file names
str7.placeholder.verify: In the page source, alt texts should describe the image instead of a file name or generic label.

str7.preload_type.title: Fix the type on image preloads
str7.preload_type.finding: A preload declares an invalid media type
str7.preload_type.explanation: Change the image preload's type value to image/jpeg, or remove the type attribute.
str7.preload_type.why: image/jpg is not a valid media type; a browser that checks the type skips the preload, so the image arrives later.
steps: Find the preloads that declare type="image/jpg" in the evidence
Change the value to image/jpeg, or remove type
Update the theme or plugin that prints it
str7.preload_type.verify: In the page source, no image preload should declare image/jpg.

str7.unsized.title: Add width and height to images
str7.unsized.finding: Images have no width and height
str7.unsized.explanation: Add width and height attributes that give each image its real proportions.
str7.unsized.why: An image with no declared size makes the page jump as it loads, which readers notice and Core Web Vitals count.
steps: Find the images with no declared size
Give each its real width and height
Use height: auto in CSS to keep it flexible
str7.unsized.verify: PageSpeed Insights should show no warning about images without explicit size.

str7.video.title: Lighten the heavy video files
str7.video.explanation: Shorten heavy videos, lower their bit rate, or host them on a video platform and embed them.
str7.video.why: A heavy video slows the page down and uses up visitors' data; on mobile in particular the page opens late.
steps: Shorten the video or lower its bit rate
Add preload="none" and a poster image
Or host it on a video platform and embed it
str7.video.verify: The Network tab of the browser's developer tools should show the video is not downloaded as the page opens.

str8.empty_table.title: Fill or remove empty tables
str8.empty_table.finding: The page contains an empty table
str8.empty_table.explanation: Put the table's content into the HTML the server sends, or remove the empty <table> element.
str8.empty_table.why: An empty table announces rows of facts and holds none. An engine that reads the page as the server sent it finds nothing in it.
steps: Find the empty table in the evidence
If a script fills it, write the rows into the server's HTML
If it is unused, remove it
str8.empty_table.verify: In the page source, the table should appear in the HTML with its rows.

str8.headers.title: Mark the header cells of data tables
str8.headers.explanation: Mark the header cells of data tables as <th>, and add scope where it helps.
str8.headers.why: Header cells say which row and column each value belongs to. Without them, engines and screen readers read the table as a run of values.
steps: Mark the table's header cells as <th>
Add scope where it helps
str8.headers.verify: In the page source, the table's header row or column should be made of <th> cells.

str8.other.title: Review table-like grids
str8.other.explanation: Rewrite <div> grids that are really data tables as <table>.
str8.other.why: Content laid out to look like a table, without being one, is harder for engines to read in the right order.
steps: Open the grids named in the evidence
Pick out those that hold rows and columns of data
Write those as a <table> with header cells
str8.other.verify: In the page source, grids that hold data should appear as <table> elements.

str8.pricing.title: Lay out price and spec comparisons as tables
str8.pricing.explanation: Write price and spec comparisons as a <table> with <th> header cells, instead of <div> grids.
str8.pricing.why: Prices and specs in a real table can be read row by row. Laid out with plain boxes, an engine cannot see which value belongs to what.
steps: Write the price or spec comparison as a <table>
Mark its header cells as <th>
str8.pricing.verify: In the page source, the comparison should sit in a <table> with <th> headers.

str9.bad_codes.title: Fix the hreflang codes
str9.bad_codes.explanation: Write hreflang values as a language code with an optional region code (for example tr or en-GB).
str9.bad_codes.why: A malformed hreflang code is ignored, so engines cannot serve that version to the right readers.
steps: Find the malformed hreflang codes in the evidence
Write the language code, plus a hyphen and region if needed (tr, en-GB)
Fix invalid forms such as underscores or language names
str9.bad_codes.verify: In the page source, every hreflang value should be a valid code such as tr or en-GB.

str9.bad_lang.title: Fix the <html lang> value
str9.bad_lang.explanation: Write the page's language in <html lang> as a valid language code (for example tr or en).
str9.bad_lang.why: A malformed language value keeps engines and screen readers from knowing the page's language.
steps: Find the malformed lang value in the evidence
Replace it with a valid code such as tr or en-GB
Fix the theme setting that prints it
str9.bad_lang.verify: In the page source, <html lang> should show a valid language code.

str9.cluster.title: Add x-default and a self link to the hreflang set
str9.cluster.finding: hreflang set lacks x-default or a self link
str9.cluster.explanation: Add the version itself and an x-default address to each language version's hreflang list.
str9.cluster.why: x-default and a link to the page itself complete the set of versions, so engines can pick one for every reader.
steps: Add each version's own address to its hreflang list
Add the default version as x-default
Keep the same list on every language version
str9.cluster.verify: In the page source, the hreflang list should include the page itself and x-default.

str9.lang_mismatch.title: Declare each page's real language
str9.lang_mismatch.finding: <html lang> does not match the content
str9.lang_mismatch.explanation: Set <html lang> to the language the page is really written in.
str9.lang_mismatch.why: The declared language tells engines which readers the page is for. A wrong one can send it to the wrong audience.
steps: Confirm the page's real language
Set <html lang> to that language
str9.lang_mismatch.verify: In the page source, <html lang> should show the page's real language.

str9.no_lang.title: Add <html lang> to pages
str9.no_lang.explanation: Add a lang attribute declaring the page's language to each page's <html> tag.
str9.no_lang.why: The declared language tells engines and screen readers what language the page is in; without it, they guess.
steps: Find the <html> tag in the theme template
Put the page's language code in the lang attribute
On a multilingual site, check the value changes per language
str9.no_lang.verify: In the page source, the <html> tag should carry a lang attribute.

str9.no_return.title: Make hreflang links reciprocal
str9.no_return.explanation: Make each language version link back with hreflang to every version that points to it.
str9.no_return.why: Language versions must point at each other. A one-way link is ignored, and engines may then show the wrong language.
steps: Find the links with no return in the evidence
Add an hreflang on the target pointing back to the source
Use the same hreflang list on every version
str9.no_return.verify: Each language version's source should show the same hreflang list pointing to the other versions.

str9.relative.title: Write hreflang addresses in full
str9.relative.explanation: Use full addresses, with protocol and domain, in hreflang links.
str9.relative.why: Google expects full addresses in hreflang; relative ones can resolve wrongly and be ignored.
steps: Find the relative hreflang addresses
Make each a full address starting with https:// and the domain
Check that the template writes full addresses
str9.relative.verify: In the page source, every hreflang address should start with https://.

str9.same_code.title: Give each hreflang code one address
str9.same_code.finding: One hreflang code is given several addresses
str9.same_code.explanation: Keep one address per language code and remove the extra ones.
str9.same_code.why: Two addresses for one language code leave engines to guess which version to show.
steps: Find the repeated hreflang codes in the evidence
Choose the right version for each code
Remove the other addresses or fix their code
str9.same_code.verify: In the page source, each hreflang code should appear only once.

str9.status.title: Fix hreflang addresses that do not work
str9.status.finding: hreflang links lead to addresses with errors
str9.status.explanation: Replace hreflang links with the version's final working address, and remove versions that do not exist.
str9.status.why: A language-version link that leads to an error tells engines about a version that is not there.
steps: Find the addresses that return an error or redirect
Replace them with the version's final working address
Remove versions that do not exist from the hreflang list
str9.status.verify: In a browser, each hreflang address should open without a redirect.

str9.target_page.title: Fix the language versions hreflang points to
str9.target_page.finding: hreflang targets are not indexable or empty
str9.target_page.explanation: Give each version hreflang points to its own title and description, and make sure it can be indexed.
str9.target_page.why: hreflang only helps for versions that can be indexed and have their own title and description; others cannot be served to readers.
steps: Give each language version its own <title> and description
Make sure the version can be indexed
Otherwise remove it from the hreflang set
str9.target_page.verify: In Search Console's URL Inspection tool, each language version should show as indexable.

tseo1.analytics_twice.title: Load the analytics tag only once
tseo1.analytics_twice.finding: The analytics tag loads more than once
tseo1.analytics_twice.explanation: Load the analytics tag from one place only (theme, plugin or tag manager) and remove the others.
tseo1.analytics_twice.why: A visit counted twice doubles page views and halves the bounce rate, so the site's own numbers mislead.
steps: Find where the tag is loaded: theme, plugin, tag manager
Keep one and remove the others
Check in the real-time report that a visit is counted once
tseo1.analytics_twice.verify: In Google Tag Assistant, each measurement ID should appear only once per page.

tseo1.blocking_scripts.title: Add defer or async to scripts in <head>
tseo1.blocking_scripts.finding: Scripts block the page from rendering
tseo1.blocking_scripts.explanation: Add defer or async to blocking scripts in <head>, or move them to the end of the page.
tseo1.blocking_scripts.why: A script in <head> without defer or async stops the page from rendering until it downloads, so content appears late.
steps: Find the scripts named in the evidence
Add async to those whose order does not matter, defer to the rest
Check that the site still works after the change
tseo1.blocking_scripts.verify: In PageSpeed Insights, these scripts should not appear under render-blocking resources.

tseo1.description_long.title: Review long meta descriptions
tseo1.description_long.finding: Meta descriptions are above the guidance band
tseo1.description_long.explanation: Shorten long meta descriptions so the first sentence says what the page offers.
tseo1.description_long.why: Character bands are editorial guidance, not Google limits or proof of a technical failure. Review clarity and usefulness in context.
steps: Read the long descriptions in a search result preview
Move the main message into the first sentence
Remove needless repetition and keyword lists
tseo1.description_long.verify: In a search result preview tool, the description's main message should show without being cut.

tseo1.description_short.title: Review short meta descriptions
tseo1.description_short.finding: Meta descriptions are below the guidance band
tseo1.description_short.explanation: Add to short meta descriptions what the page offers and what the reader gains from it.
tseo1.description_short.why: Character bands are editorial guidance, not Google limits or proof of a technical failure. Review clarity and usefulness in context.
steps: Compare the short descriptions with the page content
Add a benefit or detail specific to the page
Write a separate description for each page
tseo1.description_short.verify: In the page source, the meta description should describe the page with concrete details.

tseo1.head_closed_later.title: Move the element that ends the head early
tseo1.head_closed_later.explanation: Move the element that cannot stand in <head> into the body, and load the widget that prints it after the head tags.
tseo1.head_closed_later.why: Tags after an element that ends the head early are read as body; previews and some crawlers then miss them.
steps: Move the element named in the evidence out of <head>
Load the widget that prints it after the head tags
tseo1.head_closed_later.verify: In the page source, meta and Open Graph tags should come before the first element that ends the head.

tseo1.head_closed_lost.title: Move the element that ends the head early
tseo1.head_closed_lost.finding: <head> ends early; key tags are lost
tseo1.head_closed_lost.explanation: Move the element that cannot stand in <head> into the body, so canonical, robots and hreflang stay in the head.
tseo1.head_closed_lost.why: Google stops reading the head at the first element that cannot stand in it, so a canonical, robots or hreflang tag after it is ignored.
steps: Move the element named in the evidence out of <head>
Load the widget that prints it after the head tags
Confirm the canonical in Search Console
tseo1.head_closed_lost.verify: In Search Console's URL Inspection tool, the canonical Google selected should match the one you declared.

tseo1.heading_jumps.title: Fix skipped heading levels
tseo1.heading_jumps.explanation: Use headings in order without skipping a level, placing each subheading under the level just above it.
tseo1.heading_jumps.why: Headings in order show the page's structure; engines and screen readers use them to tell which section belongs to what.
steps: Find the skipped heading levels
Use headings in order: each subheading one level below its parent
tseo1.heading_jumps.verify: In the browser's developer tools, headings should step down in order without skipping a level.

tseo1.mixed.title: Move mixed content to https
tseo1.mixed.finding: https pages load resources over http
tseo1.mixed.explanation: Replace images, scripts and styles loaded over http:// with https:// addresses.
tseo1.mixed.why: Browsers block insecure scripts and styles on a secure page, so parts of it break or it shows as not fully secure.
steps: Find the resources loaded over http:// in the evidence
Change each to its https:// address
Host a resource that has no https yourself, or remove it
tseo1.mixed.verify: The browser console should show no mixed content warnings.

tseo1.no_viewport.title: Add a viewport meta tag to pages
tseo1.no_viewport.explanation: Add a viewport meta tag with width=device-width to the <head> of each page.
tseo1.no_viewport.why: Google indexes the mobile version of a page; without a viewport, phones show a shrunken desktop layout.
steps: Open the <head> of the theme template
Add a meta tag with name="viewport" and content="width=device-width"
Open the page on a phone and check the layout
tseo1.no_viewport.verify: The page source should show the viewport tag, and the page should open unshrunk on a phone.

tseo1.no_zoom.title: Allow readers to zoom
tseo1.no_zoom.explanation: Remove user-scalable=no and the maximum-scale limit from the viewport tag.
tseo1.no_zoom.why: Readers who need larger text cannot zoom in, which also fails an accessibility criterion.
steps: Find the viewport meta tag in the theme template
Delete user-scalable=no and maximum-scale
Try pinch-zooming the page on a phone
tseo1.no_zoom.verify: In the page source, the viewport tag should contain neither user-scalable=no nor maximum-scale.

tseo1.title_long.title: Review long page titles
tseo1.title_long.finding: Page titles are above the guidance band
tseo1.title_long.explanation: Put the page's topic first in long titles and shorten repetition and long brand suffixes.
tseo1.title_long.why: Character bands are editorial guidance, not Google limits or proof of a technical failure. Review clarity and usefulness in context.
steps: Read the long titles in a search result preview
Move the page's topic to the start of the title
Shorten repeated words and long brand suffixes
tseo1.title_long.verify: In the page source, the <title> should start with the page's topic and not repeat itself.

tseo1.title_short.title: Review short page titles
tseo1.title_short.finding: Page titles are below the guidance band
tseo1.title_short.explanation: Add the page's topic and a distinguishing detail to short titles.
tseo1.title_short.why: Character bands are editorial guidance, not Google limits or proof of a technical failure. Review clarity and usefulness in context.
steps: Compare the short titles with the page content
Add the topic and a distinguishing detail
Write a separate title for each page
tseo1.title_short.verify: In the page source, the <title> should state the page's topic clearly.

tseo1.url_decomposed.title: Rewrite addresses with composed letters
tseo1.url_decomposed.explanation: Rewrite addresses with composed or plain letters, and redirect each old address permanently to the new one.
tseo1.url_decomposed.why: A letter written as two code points makes a second address for the same word; links typed with the normal letter lead elsewhere.
steps: Rewrite each address name (the handle) in plain letters
Redirect each old address permanently to the new one
Update the links and the sitemap
tseo1.url_decomposed.verify: In the sitemap, every address should use composed characters (Unicode NFC) or plain letters.

tseo1.url_slug_unclear.title: Give pages short, readable addresses
tseo1.url_slug_unclear.explanation: Rewrite unclear slugs as a few words, and redirect each old address permanently to the new one.
tseo1.url_slug_unclear.why: A short address made of words tells visitors and engines what the page is before they open it; ids and symbols say nothing.
steps: Write each slug as a few words
Redirect each old address permanently to the new one
Update the links
tseo1.url_slug_unclear.verify: In the sitemap, addresses should be made of words, and an old address should redirect to the new one.
